artists.name: +TEK
artists.text: A producer working in the dark, driving end of electronic dance music. "Disco Necropolis (Graveyard Stage)" sounds like its title promises: a four-on-the-floor beat dressed in spooky, theatrical colour, the kind of track that turns a dance floor into a haunted level. It is pure momentum, built for moving rather than sitting still.

artists.name: 12 RODS
artists.text: 12 Rods began in Ohio and made their name after moving to Minneapolis, led by singer and guitarist Ryan Olcott. Their late-nineties records mixed indie rock with synthesizers and a sly pop sensibility, and critics loved them more than radio ever did. "Glad That It's Over" comes from 1998's Split Personalities, a warm, hooky record full of bright, odd turns.

artists.name: 90s Classics
artists.text: This is a compilation credit rather than a band, gathering songs that defined the late nineties. Its entry here is "Everybody's Free (To Wear Sunscreen)", the spoken-word hit released under Baz Luhrmann's name, built from Mary Schmich's 1997 newspaper column of advice to graduates. Gentle, funny and oddly moving, it became one of the decade's most quoted records.

artists.name: Acotto
artists.text: Acotto is a composer from the world of Japanese rhythm games. "Crossmythos Rhapsodia", written with Potwi, is a boss track from the arcade game CHUNITHM, added in 2025. Its cover art hints at hardcore, but the music leans orchestral, with jazz colour and electronic sparks racing along at a breakneck tempo, as grand and dramatic as a final battle should be.

artists.name: ADÉLA
artists.text: ADÉLA is a Slovak singer-songwriter who first reached a wide audience as a contestant on The Debut: Dream Academy, the competition that formed the group KATSEYE. Since then she has carved out her own lane in bold, theatrical pop with a sharp sense of humour. "Nicole Kidman" shows that flair: glossy, confident and built around a big personality.

artists.name: Alberto Pomeranz
artists.text: "Il barone rosso", Italian for "The Red Baron", is the track that brings Alberto Pomeranz to the Studio Lot. It is the kind of piece written to set a scene, with the drama and character of a soundtrack cue. The title conjures early aviation, dogfights above the clouds and a legendary flying ace, and the music invites you to picture the film around it.

artists.name: Alecs DeLarge
artists.text: A producer of mellow instrumental beats in the lo-fi and jazz-hop tradition. "North Street" is a gentle, unhurried track: soft drums with a little swing, warm chords and the slightly worn texture that makes this music feel like an old record playing in another room. It is made for studying, drifting or a quiet walk at dusk.

artists.name: alyzea
artists.text: alyzea makes vaporwave, the genre that slows, loops and reshapes the sounds of old commercials, malls and early computer music into something dreamy and a little uncanny. "aero plaza" fits its name, evoking glassy shopping atriums, blue skies and the glossy optimism of turn-of-the-millennium design, heard as if through a pleasant haze.

artists.name: Ametsub
artists.text: Ametsub is a Tokyo-based electronic musician whose work blends glitchy detail with piano, field recordings and a wintry, cinematic calm. His 2009 album The Nothings of the North became a quiet favourite among fans of IDM and electroacoustic music. "Snowy Lava" captures his gift for contrast: delicate, crackling textures that feel both cold and gently glowing.

artists.name: Amélie Farren
artists.text: "Unsweetened Lemonade" is the song that brings Amélie Farren to the Driftwood Shore. It is a recent release with a relaxed, sunlit feel suited to the shoreline, the kind of easygoing tune that sits well with salt air and a slow afternoon. Its title promises something bright and refreshing, with a little tartness left in.

artists.name: Ancient Chinese composer
artists.text: This credit stands in for the anonymous makers of China's oldest instrumental music. "White Snow in Early Spring" is a famous classical piece long played on the pipa and other traditional instruments, and "Imperial Concubine's Tears" carries a similar courtly, lamenting grace. These are melodies passed down through centuries, played here with plucked strings and quiet elegance.

artists.name: Andréa Daltro
artists.text: Andréa Daltro is a singer whose song "Kiuá" brings a gentle, acoustic warmth to Lanternwood. The track has the intimacy of voice and guitar, unhurried and close, the kind of song that seems to glow softly rather than shine. It is well suited to lantern light among the trees and a slow walk with nowhere to be.

artists.name: Anima Tempo
artists.text: Anima Tempo is a progressive metal band from Mexico City, known for intricate, technical songwriting in the djent tradition. Their music pairs heavy, rhythmically complex guitar work with soaring melody and atmosphere. "Primal Symmetry" shows that balance, with lockstep riffs and shifting time signatures that resolve into something grand and almost hopeful.

artists.name: Anna Sofia
artists.text: "Cruel World" is the song that places Anna Sofia in the Bedroom Pop Meadows. It has the soft, close-up feel of the genre, a voice that sounds like it is singing just to you and production that keeps things intimate rather than polished. The title hints at heartache, delivered gently and with an honest, wistful edge.

artists.name: Anthrax
artists.text: Anthrax formed in New York City in 1981 and became one of the Big Four of thrash metal alongside Metallica, Slayer and Megadeth. Famous for speed, humour and crossover experiments, including a landmark collaboration with Public Enemy, they remain a pillar of heavy music decades on. "The Edge of Perfection" carries their trademark crunch and gang-chorus energy into a new era.

artists.name: APG
artists.text: APG appears in the Nu Metal Quarry with "Embrace", a 2007 track from the heavy, emotional end of alternative metal. Expect downtuned guitars, a pounding rhythm section and a vocal that swings between brooding and cathartic, the push and pull that defined the genre through the 2000s and kept it so loud and so heartfelt.

artists.name: arai tasuku
artists.text: arai tasuku makes intricate, guitar-led music in the spirit of Japanese math rock, where clean, chiming melodies weave around shifting rhythms. "Dear Alice" has the bright, playful precision that scene is loved for, full of tapped patterns and tumbling time changes that still feel warm and tuneful rather than cold or showy.

artists.name: Arcade Player
artists.text: Arcade Player is a credit for recreations of classic video game music. Its entry here is "Cave Dweller Concert" from Donkey Kong Country, David Wise's moody, echoing cave theme from the 1994 Super Nintendo game. Recreations like this let a much-loved soundtrack be enjoyed on its own, outside the game it was written for.

artists.name: Astronaut
artists.text: A producer from the heavy, melodic side of 2010s bass music, moving between dubstep, drumstep and chillstep. Tracks like "Earthsphere VIP" pair huge, cinematic synths with crunching drops, and remixes such as "Champions - WRLD Remix" and "Rain - Calvertron Remix" show how the songs were reshaped across the scene. It is music built for big moments and bigger sound systems.

artists.name: Atoms For Peace
artists.text: Atoms For Peace began as Thom Yorke's touring band for his solo album and grew into a group of its own, with Flea, producer Nigel Godrich, drummer Joey Waronker and percussionist Mauro Refosco. Their 2013 album Amok knits live playing and electronics into restless, rhythmic grooves. "Ingenue" is one of its loveliest moments, light-footed and gently hypnotic.

artists.name: Audiobaton
artists.text: Audiobaton makes shoegaze, the genre of blurred guitars and voices melting into a wall of sound. "Alone for You" leans into that dreamy haze, with layers of reverb and distortion that feel soft rather than harsh. It is music to get lost in, like walking through fog with the light coming through.

artists.name: Audioslave
artists.text: Audioslave formed in 2001 when Soundgarden's Chris Cornell joined Tom Morello, Tim Commerford and Brad Wilk of Rage Against the Machine. Across three albums they fused Cornell's soaring voice with Morello's inventive riffs. "Like a Stone", a brooding ballad about waiting and loss, became their best-known song and one of the defining rock tracks of the 2000s.

artists.name: Axzured
artists.text: Axzured makes phonk, the genre of cowbell melodies, distorted bass and chopped Memphis rap samples that exploded online in the 2020s. "DIDDY BLUD FUNK" belongs to its meme-friendly corner, short, loud and made for viral video edits. It is music that runs on attitude and repetition, and it fits right in on the Isle of Memes.

artists.name: Beedle The Bardcore
artists.text: Beedle The Bardcore is an online creator of bardcore, the 2020s trend of reworking modern hits as if played in a medieval tavern, with lutes, recorders and archaic-sounding vocals. "Lose Yourself - Medieval Bardcore Version" turns Eminem's urgent anthem into a jaunty minstrel tune, and the joke works because the arrangement is played completely straight.

artists.name: Begin Again
artists.text: "I Ws Nvr Yr Grlfrnd" is the song that brings Begin Again to the Punk Badlands. Its stripped-down title already sets the tone: a breakup song with bite, delivered with fast guitars and a heart worn openly on the sleeve. It sits squarely in the emotional, sing-along end of punk, made to be shouted back from the crowd.

artists.name: Bell Thompson
artists.text: Bell Thompson belongs to the Small Hours, the land of late-night listening. Songs like "Always Like This" and "Most Prized" are recent releases with a quiet, reflective mood, the kind of music that suits a dim room and an unhurried mind. They feel personal and close, made for the hours when everything else has gone still.

artists.name: Ben Rosett
artists.text: Ben Rosett makes math rock, the style built from intricate guitar lines, unexpected rhythms and time signatures that twist under your feet. "Dark Energy" is a recent track with a name to match its restless drive, all interlocking patterns and sudden shifts that still find their way back to melody.

artists.name: Bill Monroe & His Blue Grass Boys
artists.text: Bill Monroe, born in Kentucky in 1911, is called the father of bluegrass, and the music took its name from his band, the Blue Grass Boys. His high, lonesome singing and fierce mandolin set the template for the genre. He wrote "Blue Moon of Kentucky" as a waltz, and Elvis Presley's 1954 rockabilly cover made it a classic twice over.

artists.name: Bioblitz
artists.text: Bioblitz appears here in the bright world of electro house and nu disco. "Globe Warmer - Farleon Remix" is a 2012 club track of punchy beats, glossy synths and a groove that keeps building, the sort of song that fills a dance floor with neon light, raised hands and momentum that never quite lets up.

artists.name: BLARF
artists.text: "Stars Without Light" is the song that places BLARF in the Sample Gardens, the land of collage, loops and found sound. The name and the title make an odd pair, playful on one side and wistful on the other, and the music lives somewhere in that gap: textured, reworked and quietly spacey.

artists.name: Blue Brew Music
artists.text: Blue Brew Music makes arrangements of well-known video game music. Its entry here is the "Wii Shop Channel" theme, the breezy bossa nova jingle from Nintendo's Wii that became a beloved internet favourite. Reworking it as a piece of its own shows how much charm was packed into a few bars of menu music.

artists.name: BLUESTEM
artists.text: BLUESTEM belongs to the Post-Punk Docklands with "Sore Eyes", a recent song with the taut, wiry energy of that scene. Expect driving bass, sharp guitar and a mood that balances tension with melody, music suited to grey skies, wet streets and walking fast with your hands in your pockets.

artists.name: Bonus Points
artists.text: Bonus Points makes lo-fi beats, the cosy instrumental hip-hop that soundtracks long study sessions. "Cup of Joe" lives up to its title: warm, mellow and comforting, with soft drums, a dusty texture and gentle chords that make it feel like a slow morning with the kettle on.

artists.name: Boowah
artists.text: Boowah appears in the Small Hours with "Nutshell", a recent song suited to late-night listening. It has an unhurried, intimate feel, the kind of track that rewards headphones and a quiet room, letting small details come forward once the rest of the world has gone to sleep.

artists.name: Bossario
artists.text: "By the Sea" is the song that carries Bossario to the Far Shores. It is a recent release with a relaxed, coastal mood, gentle and drifting, the sort of music that suits a horizon line and the slow sound of waves. Its title says it all: a calm place to sit and watch the water.

artists.name: boygenius
artists.text: boygenius is the supergroup of Julien Baker, Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus, three acclaimed American singer-songwriters who first came together on a 2018 EP. Their close harmonies and shared, confessional writing made them an instant favourite, and their 2023 album The Record won Grammys. "Me & My Dog", from that first EP, is tender, aching and quietly devastating.

artists.name: Brad Knauber
artists.text: Brad Knauber is a YouTube musician behind "Don't Mine at Night", a 2012 Minecraft parody of Katy Perry's "Last Friday Night". It turns the pop hit into a warning about creepers, zombies and the dangers of digging after dark, and it became one of the best-remembered songs of Minecraft's early YouTube era.

artists.name: BRIDEAR
artists.text: BRIDEAR is a Japanese heavy metal band formed in Fukuoka, known as an all-female group with a love of speed, melody and big, soaring choruses. Their music mixes power metal drive with J-rock flair and twin-guitar fireworks. "In The Labyrinth" shows them at full gallop, fast, dramatic and hugely tuneful.

artists.name: Brigham Phillips
artists.text: Brigham Phillips appears here with "Ratlin' Bog", a version of the traditional Irish cumulative song "The Rattlin' Bog", in which each verse adds a new link to a chain that starts with a tree in a hole in the bog. As the list grows, the song speeds up into a tongue-twisting challenge, which is exactly the fun of it.

artists.name: Béla Fleck
artists.text: Béla Fleck is an American banjo player who has spent his career showing the instrument can go anywhere, from bluegrass and newgrass to jazz, classical and African music. With New Grass Revival and his band the Flecktones he won many Grammys across different categories. "The Over Grown Waltz" shows his softer side: graceful, lilting and beautifully played.

artists.name: Camilla and the Chickens
artists.text: This is novelty music: "Forget You" performed as a chicken-clucking cover of the CeeLo Green hit. Songs like this were made for laughs, with the original melody carried by farmyard squawks, and their sheer silliness made them popular online. It is very much at home on the Isle of Memes.

artists.name: CAN
artists.text: CAN formed in Cologne in 1968 and became the most influential band of the German krautrock movement. Holger Czukay, Irmin Schmidt, Michael Karoli and Jaki Liebezeit, with singer Damo Suzuki on their classic records, built long, hypnotic grooves from improvisation and studio editing. "Halleluhwah", from 1971's Tago Mago, rides one of Liebezeit's legendary drum patterns for nearly twenty minutes.

artists.name: Cannonball Adderley
artists.text: Julian "Cannonball" Adderley was an alto saxophonist from Florida whose joyful, bluesy playing made him a star of hard bop. He played on Miles Davis's Kind of Blue before leading his own popular quintet. "Mercy, Mercy, Mercy", written by his keyboardist Joe Zawinul, became a surprise 1967 hit and a soul-jazz classic with a warm, gospel-tinged groove.

artists.name: Caramella Girls
artists.text: Caramella Girls is the animated act behind a 2008 release of "Caramelldansen", a song first recorded by the Swedish group Caramell. A sped-up version paired with a looping anime dance clip became one of the internet's first great memes, and the Caramella Girls carried that bouncy, sugar-high Europop to the charts with cartoon girls out in front.

artists.name: Careless Castle
artists.text: Careless Castle makes riddim and heavy dubstep, the stripped-back, bass-first style built on repetitive, wobbling drops and lots of space between the hits. "Echo" is a recent track that leans into that weight, with a drop designed to rattle a sound system and a mood that is dark, minimal and relentless.

artists.name: Carmen Silver
artists.text: Carmen Silver belongs to the Small Hours with "Suspended Particles", a recent song whose title suggests dust drifting in a beam of light. It has the quiet, reflective feeling of music made for the late night, unhurried and atmospheric, best heard when the room is dark and there is nowhere else to be.

artists.name: Carolina Gaitán - La Gaita
artists.text: Carolina Gaitán, known as La Gaita, is a Colombian actress and singer who voiced Pepa, the aunt whose moods change the weather, in Disney's 2021 film Encanto. She leads off "We Don't Talk About Bruno", the ensemble number that became a worldwide hit and topped the Billboard Hot 100, a rare feat for a Disney song.

artists.name: CASIOPEA
artists.text: CASIOPEA is a Japanese jazz fusion band formed in 1976, famous for virtuosic playing, bright melodies and tight, funky grooves. Led by guitarist Issei Noro, they became one of the most popular instrumental groups in Japan and a touchstone for fans of city pop and video game music. "Domino Line" here comes from a blazing 1982 concert in Tokyo.

artists.name: Catherine O'Hara
artists.text: Catherine O'Hara is a Canadian actor and comedian, celebrated for SCTV, Home Alone and Schitt's Creek. She voiced Sally, the rag doll, in Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993), and sang "Sally's Song", Danny Elfman's tender, lonely lament from the film. Her gentle, wistful performance has made it one of the soundtrack's best-loved moments.

artists.name: Cbdb
artists.text: Cbdb is a jam band from Birmingham, Alabama, known for long, winding improvisations and a warm, Southern-rooted sound that draws on rock, funk and bluegrass. Like many groups in the jam scene, they built their following on the road. "Stacy's on the Lake" has an easy, sunny swing that fits a lazy afternoon by the water.

artists.name: Ceren Yaldız
artists.text: "Ara Ara" is the track that brings Ceren Yaldız to Boom Bap Harbour. Its title is a playful phrase borrowed from anime culture, and the song pairs it with a hip-hop beat, the kind of mix of internet humour and head-nodding rhythm that travels quickly online and sticks in the head for days.

artists.name: CHAD
artists.text: This credit belongs to Chad Danforth, the basketball-loving character from Disney's High School Musical films. "I Don't Dance", from High School Musical 2 (2007), is his baseball-diamond duet with Ryan, sung by Corbin Bleu and Lucas Grabeel, as Ryan sets out to prove that dancing and sport have more in common than Chad thinks.

artists.name: Children of Zeus
artists.text: Children of Zeus is a Manchester duo, Konny Kon and Tyler Daley, who blend UK soul, R&B and hip-hop into something smooth, soulful and grounded. Their 2018 debut album Travel Light earned wide praise for its warmth and craft. "Hard Work" is a mellow, heartfelt groove about graft and keeping going, with a voice like velvet over the beat.

artists.name: Circuit Bent
artists.text: Circuit Bent makes glitch hop and bass music, full of chopped, twitching sounds and heavy low end. The name nods to circuit bending, the art of rewiring electronic toys to make strange noises. "Tonic - Mr. Bill Remix" leans into that playful precision, with the remixer's dense, detailed sound design turning every beat into a small puzzle.

artists.name: Clever Girl
artists.text: Clever Girl was a math rock band from Sheffield in England, named after the famous raptor line in Jurassic Park. Almost entirely instrumental, they released a single EP, No Drum and Bass in the Jazz Room, before splitting, and it became a cult favourite. "Elm" is one of its standouts, with interlocking guitars that build into something soaring and emotional.

artists.name: ConcernedApe
artists.text: ConcernedApe is Eric Barone, the American developer who made Stardew Valley almost entirely by himself, including its music. His four seasonal themes, from "Spring (It's a Big World Outside)" to "Winter (Nocturne of Ice)", give the farm its changing moods. Gentle, warm and a little nostalgic, they have become comfort listening for millions of players.

artists.name: CUNST
artists.text: CUNST lives on the stranger, more playful edge of the playlist. "Temporal" is a recent release from 2026, and like much of what washes up on this island it is best taken on its own terms: an odd, catchy curio that someone heard once and could not leave behind.

artists.name: Cusk
artists.text: Cusk makes small, homemade-feeling indie songs. "Blu tac piano" and "Did it make you cry" both arrived in 2026, and their titles hint at the mood: intimate, slightly scrappy and tender, the kind of music that sounds as if it was recorded in a bedroom late at night with whatever was lying around.

artists.name: Daniele Zandara
artists.text: Daniele Zandara is an Italian composer best known for his work on the soundtrack of Vampire Survivors, the hugely popular game by poncle. Pieces like "Reincarnated Echoes" and "Copper Green Intent" carry that game's mix of retro gothic drama and relentless energy, built to keep you moving through endless waves of monsters.

artists.name: Dave Era
artists.text: Dave Era makes driving, high-energy club music in the hard house tradition. "Infinite Journeys", from 2022, is built for the peak of a night: pounding kicks, rolling bass and a sense of forward motion that never lets up, the sound of a warehouse floor that has no intention of going home.

artists.name: David Maxim Micic
artists.text: David Maxim Micic is a Serbian guitarist and composer known for richly melodic progressive metal that borrows from jazz, film music and math rock. He also played in the band Destiny Potato. "Living Room" shows his playful side: intricate, shifting guitar parts that feel more like a story being told than a show of speed.

artists.name: Dazy
artists.text: Dazy is the project of James Testa from Richmond, Virginia, who writes fuzzed-out power pop with huge hooks and a punk rush. The songs are short, loud and sunny, full of buzzing guitars and sing-along choruses. "Ugly" carries that same joyful noise, sweet melodies buried under a wall of distortion.

artists.name: Dear Sherlock
artists.text: Dear Sherlock is an alternative rock duo with roots in Portugal and the UK, writing dramatic, guitar-driven songs with a strong sense of atmosphere. "Cage" has long been part of their live sets, a tense, building track that suits the winding paths of the prog lands, where songs take their time to arrive.

artists.name: DEATHNYANN
artists.text: DEATHNYANN makes sharp, intense Japanese rock. "tarantula" and "illumina", released in 2021 and 2022, pair hard-hitting guitars with dramatic vocals and quick changes of pace, the kind of urgent, colourful sound that fills the J-Rock Isles and could easily open an anime episode.

artists.name: Destiny Potato
artists.text: Destiny Potato was a Serbian progressive metal band built around guitarist David Maxim Micic and singer Aleksandra Djelmash. Their 2014 album LUN mixed heavy, rhythmic djent guitars with soaring, clear vocals and unexpected melodies. "Walls of Thoughts" captures that blend: crushing and bright at the same time.

artists.name: Dexter and The Moonrocks
artists.text: Dexter and The Moonrocks are a young Texas band who call their sound "space western": country twang and dusty Americana run through dreamy, spacey indie rock. They found a big audience online with their cosmic cowboy songs. "It's A Lot" keeps that loose, warm feel, like a ballad heard on a desert radio at night.

artists.name: Diamond Head
artists.text: Diamond Head are an English heavy metal band from the Stourbridge area, one of the key groups of the New Wave of British Heavy Metal around 1980. Their fast, riff-heavy songs hugely influenced the thrash bands that followed, most famously Metallica, who covered several of them. "Sucking My Love" is one of their early classics.

artists.name: diaphane
artists.text: diaphane is the solo electronic project of French musician Régis Baillet. His 2013 album Lifeforms, released on the German label Ant-Zen, blends deep, cinematic soundscapes with intricate beats drawn from drum and bass, dubstep and IDM. "Rhizomes" comes from that album: dark, spacious and slowly unfolding.

artists.name: Die Bokjollers
artists.text: Die Bokjollers play upbeat Afrikaans party music, the kind made for South African braais, weddings and dance floors. Their "CCR Medley" strings together Creedence Clearwater Revival favourites into one non-stop sing-along, a reminder of how much classic rock songs belong to everyone, whatever language the party is in.

artists.name: digitalluc
artists.text: digitalluc makes mellow lo-fi hip hop beats: dusty drums, soft keys and hazy samples that sit gently in the background. Tracks like "Underwater", "Driver" and "Soft Hell" date from the mid-2010s, when this sound became the soundtrack to late-night study sessions, and they still feel like a quiet room with the lights turned down.

artists.name: Direct
artists.text: Direct makes melodic electronic music, and "Hysteria" from 2013 sits squarely in the chillstep style of that era: slow, heavy bass, airy synth pads and an emotional lift that builds rather than explodes. It is music for open skies and long views, as much for drifting as for dancing.

artists.name: Diveo
artists.text: Diveo makes soft, melodic electronic music. "Summer Trees", from 2015, has the warm, glowing feel the title promises, with gentle synths and a relaxed, rolling rhythm that belongs to the mid-2010s wave of chill bass music. It suits a sunny walk through the Highlands rather than a crowded club.

artists.name: DJ Chipman
artists.text: DJ Chipman is the name credited on this version of "Peanut Butter Jelly Time", the bouncy, absurd song that became an early internet legend in the 2000s through an animation of a dancing banana. It is pure novelty: a looping beat, a chant-along hook and nothing serious about it at all.

artists.name: DJ Plead
artists.text: DJ Plead is an Australian producer whose club tracks fuse UK funky and breakbeat with percussion and rhythms from Middle Eastern music. The result is tight, rattling and hypnotic, made for dancing but full of detail. "pa700" shows that style, with crisp drums locking into a groove that keeps shifting under your feet.

artists.name: Doctor Do
artists.text: Doctor Do makes jazzy instrumental beats: warm piano chords, swung drums and the soft crackle of old records. "the world is small", from 2015, belongs to the wave of jazz-tinged lo-fi that grew up online in those years, music for slowing down, making a cup of tea and letting the afternoon drift.

artists.name: Dolphin Machine
artists.text: Dolphin Machine sits in the world of vaporwave and plunderphonics, where old pop, smooth jazz and corporate music are slowed, looped and reshaped into something dreamy and strange. "Sunshine Gradient" appears here in a remix by fellow vaporwave artist Haircuts for Men, all glossy chords and hazy, half-remembered warmth.

artists.name: Donald Byrd
artists.text: Donald Byrd was an American jazz trumpeter from Detroit who played hard bop with the greats before turning to jazz funk in the 1970s. His album Places and Spaces, produced with the Mizell brothers, became a classic of smooth, groove-led jazz. "Dominoes" from that record is one of his most sampled and loved tracks.

artists.name: Douglas Holmquist
artists.text: Douglas Holmquist is a Swedish composer known for video game soundtracks, especially the mobile games Smash Hit and PinOut, whose music moves with the player. "Hypersphere" has that same feel: shimmering synths and a steady, hypnotic pulse that sits between synthwave and ambient, perfect for gliding through misty space.

artists.name: Duke
artists.text: Duke brings the sound of Moroccan pop and rap to the dance floor. "Habibi", from 2025, blends modern beats with melodies and rhythms rooted in North African music and raï, a song built on a warm, catchy hook that works just as well at a wedding as in a club.

artists.name: Eccentric
artists.text: Eccentric makes heavy, playful bass music in the dubstep and riddim style. "funk of the week", from 2026, has the swagger its title suggests: chopped, wobbling bass and punchy drums with a funky bounce, made for big sound systems and for heads nodding hard in the front row.

artists.name: Echoflesh
artists.text: Echoflesh makes moody, nocturnal music that fits the quiet of the Small Hours. "Moonhunter", from 2020, is shadowy and slow-burning, the sort of track that suits headphones and an empty street after midnight, with a sense of something searching in the dark.

artists.name: Edgardo Nuñez
artists.text: Edgardo Nuñez is a Mexican singer and songwriter working in corridos, the storytelling ballad tradition that has been reborn with a younger, harder edge in recent years. "Renacer", meaning "to be reborn", from 2026, sets his voice within the bright guitars and swaying rhythms of modern regional Mexican music.

artists.name: Electric Joy Ride
artists.text: Electric Joy Ride makes bright, upbeat electronic dance music. "Power-Up", from 2013, lives up to its name, with sparkling melodies, a bouncing four-on-the-floor beat and a hint of video game cheer. It belongs to the early-2010s wave of feel-good electro house that spread through online music channels.

artists.name: Elena Siegman
artists.text: Elena Siegman is an American singer best known for the songs hidden in the Zombies mode of the Call of Duty games, written by composer Kevin Sherwood. Tracks like "115" and "Beauty Of Annihilation" mix heavy metal riffs with her clear, haunting vocals, and finding them in each map became a beloved ritual for players.

artists.name: Elori Saxl
artists.text: Elori Saxl is an American composer and filmmaker who blends live instruments, synthesizers and recordings of the natural world. Her album The Blue of Distance, inspired by winter on the Great Lakes, was widely praised. "Seeing Is Forgetting" has that same calm, glassy beauty: slow, layered and quietly moving.

artists.name: Enya Lisa
artists.text: Enya Lisa's recording here is a gentle take on "Only Time", the song made famous by the Irish singer Enya in 2000. It keeps the original's floating, meditative quality, a soft melody and a slow, unhurried pace, offering a moment of stillness among the long, winding jams around it.

artists.name: Eric Johnson
artists.text: Eric Johnson is a guitarist from Austin, Texas, admired for his singing, crystal-clear tone and fluid technique. "Cliffs Of Dover", from his 1990 album Ah Via Musicom, won a Grammy for Best Rock Instrumental Performance and remains one of the most celebrated guitar instrumentals ever recorded, joyful and dazzling from its first notes.

artists.name: Erika Henningsen
artists.text: Erika Henningsen is an American actress and singer who originated the role of Cady Heron in Mean Girls on Broadway in 2018, earning wide praise. "Stupid With Love" is Cady's big early number in the show, a bright, funny song about a crush scrambling her normally sharp brain.

artists.name: ERRA
artists.text: ERRA are a progressive metalcore band from Birmingham, Alabama, known for intricate, technical guitar work and a mix of harsh screams and soaring clean vocals. "House of Glass" comes from their self-titled 2021 album, heavy and precise yet full of atmosphere and melody.

artists.name: Etran de L'AÏr
artists.text: Etran de L'Aïr are a Tuareg guitar band from Agadez in Niger, playing the joyful, hypnotic desert rock of the Sahara at weddings and celebrations. Their records capture the fizzing, interlocking guitars and loose, rolling rhythms of a live party. "Imouwizla" is a fine example of that bright, circling sound.

artists.name: Express Rising
artists.text: Express Rising makes soft, textured electronic music in the IDM tradition. "Keys to Be", from 2002, is gentle and hazy, with warm tones, small glitches and a dreamlike drift that suits the Ambient Mists, the kind of track that seems to hang in the air rather than move forward.

artists.name: Ezra Collective
artists.text: Ezra Collective are a jazz group from London, led by drummer Femi Koleoso, who mix jazz with Afrobeat, hip hop, reggae and soul. In 2023 they became the first jazz act to win the Mercury Prize. Songs like "Victory Dance" are made for moving, joyful and full of brass.

artists.name: Farleon
artists.text: Farleon makes energetic electronic dance music that jumps between electro house, nu disco and dubstep. "Super Game" and the remixes from 2011 and 2012 are bright and full of punchy synths, carrying the cheerful, game-flavoured sound of the early-2010s online dance scene.

artists.name: Felipe Jara
artists.text: Felipe Jara makes lo-fi arrangements of familiar music. "Inside the Castle Walls", originally composed by Koji Kondo for Super Mario 64, becomes a soft, dusty beat here, with mellow keys and relaxed drums turning Peach's castle into a cosy place to study or unwind.

artists.name: Fernando Molinari
artists.text: Fernando Molinari is a Brazilian bassist known for virtuosic playing that blends progressive metal, jazz fusion and Latin rhythms. "Control", from his 2021 album Reaching Inside, opens with a flurry of notes before settling into an odd-meter groove, and later appeared in a session with drummer Marco Minnemann.

artists.name: Feryquitous
artists.text: Feryquitous is a Japanese composer known for fast, intricate electronic tracks, many of them written for rhythm games. His music is dense and colourful, mixing speedcore intensity with glittering melodies. "Monochrome Anomaly", featuring F9, rushes along with that restless, high-speed energy.

artists.name: Filippo Vicarelli
artists.text: Filippo Vicarelli is an Italian composer and sound designer who has been creating music and effects for video games since 2008. He is one of the composers behind the soundtrack of Vampire Survivors, and "I'm Every Reaper" comes from that world: driving, darkly playful music for being chased by Death himself.

artists.name: Fionavair
artists.text: Fionavair makes quiet, intimate music suited to the late hours. "Familyguy", from 2026, has a soft, personal feel despite its playful title, the kind of song that sounds best alone with headphones, lights low, when everyone else in the house has gone to sleep.

artists.name: First Fragment
artists.text: First Fragment are a technical death metal band from Quebec, famous for blending brutal heaviness with dazzling neoclassical guitar, flamenco touches and fretless bass. Their 2016 album Dasein is a cult favourite among fans of extreme virtuoso music. "Prélude En Sol Dièse Mineur" shows their more classical, elegant side.

artists.name: First of October
artists.text: First of October plays math rock, the style of tricky time signatures and bright, tapping guitar lines. "Ravioli", from 2019, keeps things light and playful, a fittingly silly title for a track full of twisting rhythms and cheerful, knotted melodies.

artists.name: FLat7
artists.text: FLat7 makes dreamy, soft-focus music in the shoegaze and dream pop vein. "パス・トゥ・ハート", meaning "Path to Heart", from 2012, wraps a gentle Japanese melody in shimmering guitars and hazy reverb, sounding like a memory seen through fogged glass.

artists.name: Floral
artists.text: Floral are an instrumental math rock duo from the San Francisco Bay Area: guitarist Nate Sherman and drummer Ty Mayer. Their music is bright, intricate and full of tapping, bending guitar lines over nimble drums. "Marsh Partition" opens their 2015 EP, a short, sparkling burst of their tangled style.

artists.name: FM-84
artists.text: FM-84 is the synthwave project of Col Bennett, whose 2016 album Atlas became one of the defining records of the genre. With the singer Ollie Wride, it captures a golden, sunset-drenched vision of the 1980s. "Arcade Summer" is an instrumental highlight, all shimmering synths and endless summer nostalgia.

artists.name: Fonola Band
artists.text: Fonola Band is a name found on recordings of familiar songs, and here it offers a version of "Bella ciao", the Italian folk song sung by partisans who resisted fascism in the Second World War. Simple and rousing, it has become an anthem of resistance and hope sung all over the world.

artists.name: For Opal
artists.text: For Opal makes guitar-driven alternative rock with a moody, melodic edge. "Fatal Attraction", from 2025, has the push and pull its title suggests, building tension between brooding verses and a bigger, fuller sound, at home on the windswept Alt Rock Moors.

artists.name: Fort Minor
artists.text: Fort Minor was the hip hop side project of Mike Shinoda of Linkin Park, whose album The Rising Tied came out in 2005. "Remember the Name", featuring Styles of Beyond, is a pounding anthem about the work behind success that has since become a fixture in sports highlights and workout playlists.

artists.name: Francesco Farfa
artists.text: Francesco Farfa is an Italian DJ and producer whose career runs back to the 1990s dance scene. "Universal Love", from 2010, is euphoric and open-hearted, built on soaring melodies and a steady pulse that carries the warm, hands-in-the-air spirit of classic trance and house.

artists.name: Francis Mercier
artists.text: Francis Mercier is a Haitian-American DJ and producer known for afro house that blends deep, hypnotic grooves with Caribbean and African influences. He also runs his own label, Deep Root Records. "Unjust", from 2026, shows his signature mix of rich percussion, melody and quiet emotion.

artists.name: Funk Factory - Michael Urbaniak
artists.text: Funk Factory was a 1970s jazz funk band formed with the Polish jazz violinist Michał Urbaniak, a pioneer of electric violin in jazz. Their music mixes tight funk grooves with adventurous jazz improvisation. "Rien Ne Va Plus", from 1976, captures that combination of swagger and skill.

artists.name: Geek Music
artists.text: Geek Music releases covers of famous themes from television, films, games and anime. Here it brings the "Jeopardy!" main theme, the instantly recognisable countdown music from the long-running American quiz show, which has become shorthand for waiting and thinking all over the world.

artists.name: Ginger Root
artists.text: Ginger Root is the project of Californian musician Cameron Lew, who writes, plays and films nearly everything himself. He calls his style "aggressive elevator soul": warm keys, tight bass and a big affection for Japanese city pop of the 1980s. "Loretta" became his breakout, a breezy, grinning groove that sounds like a lost broadcast from a sunnier decade.

artists.name: Glasshouse Red Spider Mite
artists.text: Glasshouse Red Spider Mite are a young band from Brighton, formed in 2023, whose debut EP arrived at the end of 2025. Their songs move slowly and carefully, with knotted guitars and breathy, close-up vocals. "Ride or Die" is a love song at heart, taking a slightly silly phrase and finding something honest underneath it.

artists.name: Gost
artists.text: Gost is an American producer of darksynth, the heavier, more sinister corner of synthwave. His music pairs pulsing 1980s synthesizers with horror-film menace and, at times, the weight of metal. "Genesee Avenue" comes from his 2015 output, a driving, neon-lit track that feels like a chase scene through an empty city at night.

artists.name: Hailey Picardi
artists.text: Hailey Picardi is a young singer-songwriter whose debut EP, scars to prove it, explores healing and the tangled way we sometimes love what hurts us. "chaotic" opens that record and gave it its name. Raw and confessional, it keeps a short moment of her talking at the start, as if you have wandered into the room while it was being made.

artists.name: Halo
artists.text: This credit gathers music from the Halo video game series, whose choral, orchestral scores became some of the most recognisable in gaming, originally composed by Martin O'Donnell and Michael Salvatori. "Breaking the Covenant" comes from the music for 2014's Halo 2 Anniversary, pairing soaring strings with heavy, driving rock guitars built for a battle.

artists.name: Hampton The Hampster
artists.text: Hampton the Hampster is the cartoon star of the Hampster Dance, one of the internet's first viral sensations: a 1998 web page full of dancing animated hamsters looping a sped-up tune. In 2000 it became a real single, "The HampsterDance Song," produced by Canada's Boomtang Boys. Squeaky, relentless and impossibly cheerful, it is a true artefact of the early web.

artists.name: HANABIE.
artists.text: HANABIE. are an all-woman metalcore band from Tokyo who call their sound "Harajuku-core", mixing breakdowns and screams with bright pop hooks and playful energy. They formed in 2015 and later signed with Epitaph Records. "お先に失礼します。" (roughly "Excuse me for leaving first") turns the dread of overtime at work into a furious, gleeful anthem.

artists.name: Haute & Freddy
artists.text: Haute & Freddy are a Los Angeles duo, singer Michelle Buzz and drummer Lance Shipp, who blend 1980s synth-pop with a theatrical, vintage-circus look. They signed with Atlantic Records and released their debut album, Big Disgrace, in 2026. "Femme Hysteria" comes from that record, a glossy, dramatic pop song with a dark streak running through it.

artists.name: hey, nothing
artists.text: hey, nothing are an emo-folk duo from Georgia whose music sits between acoustic intimacy and the swell of Midwest emo. Their debut album, Hound, arrived in 2026. "Arteries" closes it, a song about friendship and growing pains that slowly builds until everything bursts open, like a long-held breath finally let go.

artists.name: hitohira
artists.text: hitohira are a four-piece indie rock band from Tokyo, formed in 2021, who draw on math rock, emo and shoegaze. Their songs pair intricate, ringing guitars with gentle Japanese melodies and abstract, dreamy lyrics. "That Scene" catches that balance, its busy fretwork and soft haze meeting somewhere between precision and daydream.

artists.name: Hollywood Studio Orchestra
artists.text: The Hollywood Studio Orchestra is a recording credit used for orchestral performances of famous film music, rather than a band with a public story. Its releases re-record beloved themes for listeners who want the big-screen sound at home. Here it plays the "Indiana Jones Theme," John Williams's swashbuckling march that still sounds like adventure itself.

artists.name: Home
artists.text: Home is the synthwave project of American producer Randall Taylor, whose 2014 album Odyssey became a cult favourite across the vaporwave and chillwave world. His music is soft-focus and nostalgic, all warm synths and drifting melodies that feel like a half-remembered evening. "Nosebleed" comes from that same album, hazy and gently propulsive.

artists.name: Hoshikuma Minami
artists.text: Hoshikuma Minami is a Japanese singer who has carved out a loud, heavy rock sound of her own, making room for girls who don't fit the role of the polished heroine. Her songs pair crushing guitars with soaring vocals built for the energy of live shows. "CRAVE" is one of her earlier tracks, while "OXYGEN" was written with crowds in mind.

artists.name: Hue Hinton
artists.text: Hue Hinton's "I Crashed My Car" sits among the slow, hazy songs of the Shoegaze Fens, where guitars blur at the edges and vocals drift just beneath the surface. The title alone hints at a bruised, confessional mood. It is the kind of track that rewards listening on headphones with the lights turned low.

artists.name: Hybrid Minds
artists.text: Hybrid Minds are a British duo who became one of the best-loved names in liquid drum and bass. Their tracks pair rolling, fast breakbeats with lush pads, piano and tender vocals, so the music feels both urgent and calm at once. "Touch" is a fine example, smooth and emotional, built for both dancefloors and late-night drives.

artists.name: I Hate My Village
artists.text: I Hate My Village is an Italian supergroup bringing together Adriano Viterbini, Fabio Rondanini, Alberto Ferrari of Verdena and Marco Fasolo. Their 2019 debut fused West African guitar styles with psychedelic, angular rock and tight, hypnotic drumming. "Tony Hawk of Ghana" shows off that mix, playful and wiry, with riffs that circle and skip like a skater.

artists.name: Ichika Nito
artists.text: Ichika Nito is a Japanese guitarist celebrated online for his clean, sparkling tapping technique and dreamy chord voicings. His short videos made him a favourite among guitarists around the world, and his instrumentals blend math rock precision with a delicate, almost glassy beauty. "The Moon's Elbow" carries that touch, intricate yet calm, like light on water.

artists.name: Idealism
artists.text: Idealism makes lo-fi hip hop in its gentlest form: dusty drums, soft piano and jazz chords, and the crackle of old records. Track titles like "monster gambling in tokyo" and "waon to ame" hint at a fondness for Japan and quiet, rainy evenings. This is music made for studying, unwinding or simply staring out of a window.

artists.name: il:lo
artists.text: il:lo is an electronic duo known for intricate, atmospheric soundscapes that blend downtempo, trip hop and ambient music. Their work has appeared on Anjunadeep, a label known for deep, emotional electronic music. "Reine" carries their slow-moving warmth, with layered textures and patient beats that unfold like a city waking up at dawn.

artists.name: Infinity Shred
artists.text: Infinity Shred are an instrumental group from New York City who mix synthwave, electronic music and progressive metal into something bright and cinematic. "Long May You Run" was the first single from their 2019 album Forever, A Fast Life, released on Periphery's 3DOT Recordings. It feels like a retro-futuristic sprint toward the horizon.

artists.name: Insan3lik3
artists.text: Insan3lik3 is a Swiss producer based in Zurich, known for funky, upbeat electronic music with euphoric melodies and bouncy grooves. Releases on labels like Monstercat helped his tracks reach millions of listeners in the early 2010s. "Bad Pitched" catches that era's energy, heavy bass wobbles and bright synths in playful conversation.

artists.name: International Music System
artists.text: International Music System was an Italian studio project created in 1983 in Vicenza by Maurizio Cavalieri and Giorgio Stefani, also behind Charlie's "Spacer Woman." Their records mixed Italo disco with early electro, and their self-titled album is now a prized collector's item. "Mojave" carries that sound, cool synthesizers and robotic rhythms built for a futuristic dancefloor.

artists.name: ivri
artists.text: ivri is an American singer-songwriter whose music has moved from confessional electronic bedroom pop toward a darker, shoegaze-leaning rock sound. Her songs pair intimate, close-up vocals with walls of fuzzy guitar and moments of real catharsis. "NOISE" belongs to that heavier side, letting distortion swell around her voice until the two seem to blur.

artists.name: James Egbert
artists.text: James Egbert is an American electronic producer whose music became a staple of the early Monstercat label. His tracks blend dubstep weight with electro house drive and big, emotional melodies. "Halo" from 2012 is a favourite from that era, building from shimmering synths into a heavy drop that still sounds like the best of that moment.

artists.name: Jamws
artists.text: "Toronto" by Jamws sits in the Hip-Hop Boroughs, a track named for the Canadian city whose sound has shaped so much modern rap and R&B. Expect a moody, late-night atmosphere and a strong sense of place in the title. It is a small, personal entry in a land full of big voices.

artists.name: Jessie Mazin
artists.text: Jessie Mazin is a singer-songwriter whose debut EP, untitled.jpeg, turned personal chaos into honest, open-hearted songs about connection. Her writing is direct and unguarded, delivered in a voice that feels close and conversational. "the precipice" captures that standing-at-the-edge feeling, quiet and suspended, the moment before everything changes.

artists.name: Jimmy Smith
artists.text: Jimmy Smith was the American organist who made the Hammond B-3 a star of jazz, blending bebop, blues and gospel into soul jazz from the 1950s onward. Root Down, recorded live in Los Angeles in 1972, is one of his funkiest records. Its title track, "Root Down (And Get It)", was later famously sampled by the Beastie Boys.

artists.name: Jinsang
artists.text: Jinsang is a producer from the heart of the lo-fi hip hop wave of the mid-2010s, when mellow beats spread across YouTube and SoundCloud. His music is warm and unhurried, with soft keys, jazzy samples and gently swinging drums. "Genesis" is a quiet, glowing piece, the sort of beat that makes a rainy afternoon feel like a gift.

artists.name: Joe Henderson
artists.text: Joe Henderson was an American tenor saxophonist with a distinctive, searching sound, known for classic Blue Note records like Page One. In 1974 he recorded The Elements with harpist and pianist Alice Coltrane, a spiritual jazz album with pieces named for fire, air, water and earth. "Earth" is a deep, grounding piece, rich with percussion and meditative calm.

artists.name: Joe Siris
artists.text: "It's Okay to Leave a Dog in a Hot Car" is a comedy song whose deliberately outrageous title is the whole joke, a piece of internet absurdism that circulated as a meme. Joe Siris is the name credited with it. It belongs on the Isle of Memes, where songs are less about the music than the shared laughter.

artists.name: John Cena
artists.text: John Cena, the WWE wrestler turned actor, released "The Time Is Now" in 2005 on his rap album You Can't See Me, made with his cousin Tha Trademarc. The song became his entrance music, and its trumpet blast later became one of the internet's best-known memes, popping up unexpectedly in countless prank videos.

artists.name: John Luther
artists.text: "Inhale" by John Luther sits in the Small Hours, a land of quiet songs for late nights and long thoughts. As its title suggests, it feels like a song about slowing down and catching your breath. It suits a moment of stillness, when the world is asleep and there is room to think.

artists.name: Jon Keith
artists.text: Jon Keith is an American singer and rapper whose music blends hip hop, R&B and Christian faith, and he has been mentored by producer Rodney "Darkchild" Jerkins. "YOU CAN ALWAYS COME BACK HOME," featuring Chance the Rapper, is a warm invitation to anyone weighed down by shame or regret: a song about taking the first step back.

artists.name: Jonny Abbey
artists.text: Jonny Abbey's "The Superb Lyrebird" blends lo-fi beats with jazz chords and soft, unhurried rhythms. Its title nods to the Australian bird famous for mimicking almost any sound it hears, a fitting image for beat-making built on samples. It is gentle, curious music for quiet afternoons in the Lo-Fi Hills.

artists.name: Josie on the Rocks
artists.text: Josie on the Rocks is a band fronted by Lily Cornell Silver, daughter of Soundgarden's Chris Cornell. "Not You" was the first song the band wrote together, a sultry, soulful take on a toxic relationship. It was released as a tribute to the band's late drummer, Graham Derzon-Supplee, which gives it an added tenderness.

artists.name: jungle wizard
artists.text: jungle wizard makes jungle, the fast, breakbeat-driven music that grew out of 1990s British rave culture. "Peace Within Colors" leans to the gentler side of the style, with chopped-up drums racing beneath soft, colourful pads. The contrast between frantic rhythm and calm melody makes it feel both energised and serene.

artists.name: Just Neighbors
artists.text: Just Neighbors are a mostly instrumental math rock band from Gainesville, Florida. Their music weaves intricate, interlocking guitars with odd time signatures and the warm, emotional pull of Midwest emo and post-rock. "L I G H T" lets those patterns bloom slowly, bright and hopeful, like sunlight through a window.

artists.name: Kaelin Ellis
artists.text: Kaelin Ellis is an American producer and multi-instrumentalist from Florida, known for hip hop, electronic and jazz-funk, and for viral videos of fast, inventive beat-making. His influences include Madlib and J Dilla, and his music is full of rich keys and crisp, bouncing drums. "Move" shows his groove-first style, funky and loose.

artists.name: Kahoot!
artists.text: Kahoot! is the quiz game used in classrooms around the world, and its lobby music is one of the most recognisable tunes for a generation of students. The bouncy, looping theme plays while players join a game, and "Lobby Music (Original Soundtrack)" instantly brings back the thrill and panic of a pop quiz.

artists.name: KatzPascale
artists.text: KatzPascale's songs drift through the Ambient Mists, where music tends toward slow, enveloping textures. Titles like "SINK WHERE YOU SLEEP" and "SPILL YOUR TIME" suggest heavy, dreamlike moods about rest and letting go. These are pieces to sink into rather than follow, quiet and immersive.

artists.name: Keo
artists.text: Keo is a London rock act fronted by singer Finn Keogh, whose debut album, Put A Smile On For Me, came out on Island Records in 2026. "That's Me," its lead single, is a grungy, snarling song about letting go of the guilt of keeping a secret, with distorted guitars and plenty of attitude.

artists.name: Kevin Sherwood
artists.text: Kevin Sherwood is a composer and sound designer at Treyarch, best known for the hidden songs of the Call of Duty Zombies mode, which players unlock by finding secret objects on each map. "Lullaby Of A Deadman," sung by Elena Siegman, is one of the earliest and most beloved, a heavy, melancholy rock ballad.

artists.name: KIRBY
artists.text: KIRBY is an American singer-songwriter from Mississippi known for warm, Southern-tinged soul and R&B, who earlier co-wrote songs for major stars, including Rihanna's "FourFiveSeconds." "Saving Grace" is her theme for the series Spider-Noir, set in a 1930s noir world. Its melancholy soul feels like a smoky jazz club after dark.

artists.name: Klaus Johann Grobe
artists.text: Klaus Johann Grobe are a Swiss duo who blend krautrock's steady, hypnotic rhythms with vintage organ, disco grooves and German-language vocals. Their music is playful and stylish, both hazy and danceable. "Discogedanken", meaning roughly "disco thoughts", captures their charm, a sleek, looping groove that feels like a daydream in motion.

artists.name: Krystyna Prońko
artists.text: Krystyna Prońko is a Polish singer whose career has spanned decades, known for a rich, soulful voice and music touched by jazz, soul and pop. "Jesteś lekiem na całe zło" ("You are the cure for all evil") is one of her most beloved songs, a warm, timeless ballad that remains a classic of Polish popular music.

artists.name: Kyegi
artists.text: Kyegi works in IDM, the restless, detailed side of electronic music where glitches, odd rhythms and intricate sound design take centre stage. "Tl.return" fits that tradition, with stuttering textures and shifting patterns that reward close listening. It is music for exploring rather than dancing, full of tiny surprises.

artists.name: LAOS
artists.text: LAOS are a drum and bass crew from Helsinki, Finland, known for melodic, liquid-leaning tracks and releases on labels such as Hospital and Viper. In 2007 they also remixed 4hero. "Panda Style" is a smooth, rolling liquid piece, with crisp breakbeats and soulful warmth, made for long, flowing journeys.

artists.name: Latarnik
artists.text: Latarnik is the solo name of Marek Pędziwiatr, a pianist, composer and synth player from Wrocław, Poland, best known from the bands EABS and Błoto. His music blends jazz with ambient textures and electronic warmth. "Insia" is a gentle, floating piece, where soft keys and calm grooves drift together.

artists.name: Left Tracks
artists.text: Left Tracks are a California duo, Phil Di Leo in Oakland and Kabir Kumar in Los Angeles, who write together across hundreds of miles. Their music is hazy and textured, built from layered guitars and soft vocals. "Popcorn Lung" drifts in the Shoegaze Fens, where blurry guitars and dreamlike moods make a natural home.

artists.name: LeviathanJPTV
artists.text: LeviathanJPTV is a YouTube creator best known for "Chug Jug With You," a parody of Estelle's "American Boy" written about the video game Fortnite. It went viral in 2021, sung earnestly by countless fans online. Its completely sincere tribute to video game victories made it a lasting meme.

artists.name: Life of the Party
artists.text: Life of the Party's "Ooh Child" is a cover of "O-o-h Child," the 1970 soul classic by the Five Stairsteps. The original is a gentle promise that things will get easier, and it has been reinterpreted many times. This version brings that warm reassurance to the Soul Lowlands, a song of comfort that never goes out of style.

artists.name: Lilac Stranger
artists.text: Lilac Stranger plays math rock with an edge of mathcore and post-hardcore, where tangled guitar lines and sudden rhythm changes collide. "Bubble Party!" lives up to its playful title, bursting with jittery energy and bright, darting riffs. It is a restless, exciting track that rarely stays in one place for long.

artists.name: Lily Meola
artists.text: Lily Meola is a singer-songwriter raised on Maui, Hawaii, who won a Golden Buzzer on America's Got Talent with an original song. Her music is heartfelt and acoustic-led, with a warm, soulful voice and touches of folk and country. "You and I" carries that sincere warmth, simple and open-hearted.

artists.name: Ling tosite sigure
artists.text: Ling tosite sigure are a trio from Saitama, Japan, formed in 2002: TK on guitar and vocals, 345 on bass and vocals, and Pierre Nakano on drums. Their explosive, complex songs fuse math rock, post-hardcore and pop melody. "abnormalize" opened the anime Psycho-Pass, and "Enigmatic Feeling" its second season.

artists.name: Liquid Tension Experiment
artists.text: Liquid Tension Experiment is an instrumental supergroup of Mike Portnoy, John Petrucci, Jordan Rudess and Tony Levin, formed in the late 1990s and closely tied to Dream Theater. Their music is dazzling progressive metal, packed with virtuoso solos and complex time signatures. "Biaxident," from their 1999 second album, shows their dexterity.

artists.name: Lou Doe
artists.text: A newer name on the garage side of the playlist, Lou Doe turns up here with "Andrew's Favorite," a 2026 release. The song sits on Garage Rock Row among scrappy guitars and loose, live-sounding energy, and its title has the feel of a tune written for a friend. Play it loud and let it rattle the walls.

artists.name: Loukeman
artists.text: Loukeman arrives on the dance floor of the Four-on-the-Floor Steppe with "Elktorn," released in 2026. It belongs to the land of steady kick drums and long, rolling builds, music made for moving rather than sitting still. The title hints at something wild and northern, a fitting soundtrack for open grassland under a pulsing sky.

artists.name: LSD and the Search for God
artists.wiki: LSD and the Search for God

artists.name: M@cky88
artists.text: M@cky88 makes hazy, guitar-washed music in the dream pop and shoegaze tradition, the kind where vocals melt into a fog of reverb and distortion. "Hail Mary," a 2026 release, brings that blurred, glowing sound to the Shoegaze Fens, where it fits right in among the mist and soft feedback.

artists.name: Madska
artists.text: Drifting into the Shoegaze Fens is Madska's "More Than Dramatic," a 2026 song that sits among the playlist's dreamiest, most reverb-soaked music. Its title promises big feeling, and the land around it answers with slow waves of sound and soft light. A good song to stand still for and let wash over you.

artists.name: Manteeny
artists.text: Manteeny's "One Two - Original Mix" is a 2013 club track, and the "Original Mix" tag marks it as the producer's own version rather than a remix, as dance releases often do. It lives in the Electro Foundry, home of punchy synths and hard-hitting electronic beats built to fill a dance floor.

artists.name: Martin Luther King, Jr.
artists.text: Baptist minister Martin Luther King, Jr. was the most prominent leader of the American civil rights movement and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964. "I Have A Dream" is his speech from the 1963 March on Washington, delivered before the Lincoln Memorial to a crowd of hundreds of thousands. It remains one of the most famous speeches ever given.

artists.name: Maybsomeday
artists.text: Maybsomeday plays heavy, hook-driven music that sits where metalcore meets pop punk, mixing breakdown weight with big, singable choruses. Their 2023 song "Zombie" brings that blend to the Metalcore Caldera, where crushing guitars and soaring melodies share the same fiery ground.

artists.name: meganeko
artists.text: meganeko is an electronic producer known for bright, playful tracks that borrow the sounds of video games and chiptune and push them through heavy, polished electro. Songs like "Astro Soda" and "Sharkatzor" show a sense of humour as much as production skill. In the Electro Foundry, this music sounds like an arcade cabinet running at full power.

artists.name: Melano
artists.text: Melano's "On Fire" is a 2016 bass track rooted in drum and bass and drumstep, the style that pairs fast, rolling rhythms with heavy, half-time drops. It belongs on the Liquid Rapids, where the music moves as quickly as the water, all momentum and spray.

artists.name: Memo Boy
artists.text: Memo Boy's "Facebook.com" is a 2021 track from the IDM Glitchlands, a land of chopped-up beats, stuttering samples and electronic music that likes to break its own rules. With a title borrowed from a website address, it fits a corner of the world where the internet itself is part of the texture.

artists.name: Michael Lementi
artists.text: Michael Lementi's songs here share their names with two famous video game themes: "Aquatic Ambience" from Donkey Kong Country and "Big Blue" from F-Zero. Released in 2015 and 2016, they live in the Lo-Fi Hills, where game music is often slowed down and softened into warm, unhurried listening for late nights.

artists.name: MicroDragon
artists.text: MicroDragon's "Bill Nye The Science Guy" is a 2019 track named after the beloved science television show and its famously shouty theme. It lives on the Isle of Memes, where internet humour and remix culture rule, and music is as likely to make you laugh as to make you dance.

artists.name: Mitsukiyo
artists.text: Mitsukiyo is a Korean composer who writes in a blend of jazz, electronic and pop styles and is known for background music for the mobile game Blue Archive. "Irodori Canvas - Korean Version" is a 2024 release, a bright, colourful song that fits the energetic, anime-flavoured mood of the J-Rock Isles.

artists.name: MONO
artists.text: MONO are an instrumental post-rock band from Tokyo, formed in 1999 and known for vast, orchestral songs that swell from near silence into overwhelming walls of guitar. "Ashes in the Snow" opens their 2009 album Hymn to the Immortal Wind, and it is a perfect introduction to their slow-burning, cinematic sound.

artists.name: Moth Equals
artists.text: Moth Equals is a British producer who makes dark, moody electronica rooted in trip hop and downtempo. "Jeunesse," French for youth, comes from the EP One Tusk, a record of slow beats and sentimental atmospheres. In the Trip-Hop Undercity, its hazy, after-hours feel finds a natural home.

artists.name: Mr. Bill
artists.text: Mr. Bill is an Australian electronic producer famous for intricate, hyper-detailed glitch and IDM, and for teaching music production through tutorials and his long-running podcast. Tracks like "Pish Posh" and the tongue-in-cheek "IDM Anthem" show off his playful sound design, where every snare and squelch seems to have been sculpted by hand.

artists.name: Mulatu Astatke
artists.text: Mulatu Astatke is the Ethiopian vibraphonist and composer known as the father of Ethio-jazz, a sound that blends Ethiopian scales and melodies with jazz and Latin rhythms. "Yègellé Tezeta" is one of his best-loved recordings, and his music reached a new audience through the Éthiopiques series and the 2005 film Broken Flowers.

artists.name: my bloody valentine
artists.text: Formed in Dublin in 1983 and led by Kevin Shields, my bloody valentine made the defining record of shoegaze with their 1991 album Loveless. "Only Shallow" and "When You Sleep" both come from it, built from bending, blurred guitar and half-buried vocals. Few records have shaped the sound of dreamy, noisy rock as deeply.

artists.name: Myon
artists.text: Myon is a Hungarian DJ and producer, known first as half of the trance duo Myon & Shane 54 before continuing on his own. "Omen In The Rain" appears here in a Seven Lions remix, which blends Myon's melodic trance with Seven Lions' sweeping, bass-heavy style, a natural fit for the Trance Steppe.

artists.name: NEMOPHILA
artists.text: NEMOPHILA are a Japanese all-female heavy metal band formed in 2019, known for fast, technical playing and powerful vocals. "REVIVE" and "鬼灯" (Hōzuki) date from 2021, mixing crushing riffs with catchy melodies and touches of traditional Japanese flavour. On the Power Metal Peaks, their energy is right at home.

artists.name: Nerv
artists.text: Nerv are a genre-bending heavy rock band from the Sacramento area, mixing metalcore weight with big, modern rock hooks. "Not The One" comes from their 2022 debut album We're All Patients Here. In the Metalcore Caldera, it adds a punchy, radio-ready edge to the heat and the noise.

artists.name: Nico Play
artists.text: Nico Play's "La Ciruela" is a 2022 song from the Latin Coast, where the music is warm, rhythmic and made for dancing in the sun. The title means "the plum" in Spanish, a playful, juicy image that matches the land's easygoing, sunlit mood.

artists.name: NINA
artists.text: NINA is a German-born singer and songwriter based in London and one of the best-known voices of modern synthwave, pairing glossy 1980s-style synths with heartfelt pop melodies. "Beyond Memory" is a 2016 song that captures her nostalgic, neon-lit sound. She often works with Radio Wolf, whose music sits nearby on the Synthwave Coast.

artists.name: Noah Gallagher
artists.text: The pieces here from Noah Gallagher, "Whiteout," "The Gauntlet" and "Doctrine Factorum," were released between 2023 and 2026 and live in the Small Hours. Their titles suggest snowblind stillness, hard-won trials and something almost ceremonial, music that rewards listening closely when the world has gone quiet.

artists.name: Normandie
artists.text: Normandie are a Swedish rock band who blend metalcore heft with polished, melodic choruses. "Blood In The Water" is a 2023 song that shows off that balance, with heavy guitars driving big, emotional hooks. It sits among the Metalcore Caldera's loudest and most anthemic music.

artists.name: NOTHING MORE
artists.text: NOTHING MORE are a rock band from San Antonio, Texas, known for heavy, inventive alternative metal and vocalist Jonny Hawkins' intense performances. "Fade In / Fade Out" comes from their 2017 album The Stories We Tell Ourselves, which earned them Grammy nominations, while "VALHALLA (Too Young To See)" arrived in 2022.

artists.name: NOVELISTS
artists.text: NOVELISTS are a French progressive metalcore band from Paris, known for technical, djent-flavoured guitar work and soaring melodic choruses. "Ravage" dates from their early years, while "Antares" shows how their sound has grown more expansive. Their precise, intricate heaviness makes them a fixture of the Metalcore Caldera.

artists.name: o k h o
artists.text: Dusty drum loops, softened keys and gentle crackle: o k h o makes lo-fi hip hop, the kind of music made for studying or drifting off. "41058" is a 2016 track with a title of nothing but numbers, which suits a style that lets mood speak louder than words. It belongs in the calm of the Lo-Fi Hills.

artists.name: Of The Trees
artists.text: Of The Trees is the bass music project of producer and visual artist Tyler Coombs, originally from Maine and based in Denver. His music blends heavy low end with organic, nature-inspired sound design. "Windhorse" featuring Sophie Marks opened his 2021 EP The Tale of Elegos, a dreamy, downtempo turn that shows his gentler side.

artists.name: Omnitica
artists.text: Omnitica's "Yo! Ho! And a Bottle of Bass!" is a 2011 dubstep track whose title swaps rum for bass in the old pirate song. It comes from the early, wobble-heavy era of dubstep and drumstep, and it brings a swashbuckling, tongue-in-cheek energy to the jagged ground of the Dubstep Shards.

artists.name: Orange Dog Club
artists.text: Orange Dog Club bring "running out of time" to Garage Rock Row, a 2026 song with a lowercase title and the restless feel of a band playing in a small room. The land is all fuzz, energy and rough edges, and this song carries that urgency right in its name.

artists.name: OUT IN FRONT
artists.text: OUT IN FRONT's "Medicine" is a 2026 song from the Alt Rock Moors, a land of big guitars, open skies and emotional choruses. Its title suggests music as a cure, which is exactly how a lot of alternative rock is meant to be heard: loud, honest and a little healing.

artists.name: Outrun The Sunlight
artists.text: Outrun The Sunlight are an instrumental progressive band from Chicago who combine the weight of progressive metal with the atmosphere of post-rock. "Red Bird" is the title track and opener of their 2017 album, building slowly from spacey, ambient beginnings into heavily layered climaxes. Its patience suits the Djent Spires well.

artists.name: Owl City
artists.text: Owl City is the project of Adam Young from Owatonna, Minnesota, who rose to fame in 2009 with the dreamy electropop hit "Fireflies." "Good Time," his bright 2012 duet with Carly Rae Jepsen, became another major hit. Sparkling, cheerful and impossible to sit still to, it suits the Glitterlands perfectly.

artists.name: Oysterhead
artists.text: Oysterhead is a supergroup of Primus bassist Les Claypool, Phish guitarist Trey Anastasio and Police drummer Stewart Copeland. "Rubberneck Lions" comes from their only album, The Grand Pecking Order, released in 2001. Quirky, funky and full of virtuoso interplay, it is a cult favourite in the Jam Band Commonwealth.

artists.name: Pat's Soundhouse
artists.text: Pat's Soundhouse brings "Eggshell Song" to Mount Virtuoso, the land of skilled playing and ambitious musicianship. Released in 2026, the song's title suggests something delicate, music that treads carefully before it shows what it can do. It is a small, curious piece among the mountain's showpieces.

artists.name: Patryk Scelina
artists.text: Patryk Scelina's "Fondue los Muertos" is a 2026 piece that lives on the Game Isles, among soundtracks and music written for play. Its title, a playful mash of melted cheese and the Day of the Dead, promises something lively and a little mischievous, like the theme of a festive level.

artists.name: Pendulum
artists.text: Pendulum formed in Perth, Australia, and became one of the biggest names in drum and bass, fusing it with rock guitars and live energy. "Witchcraft" comes from their 2010 album Immersion, which reached number one in the UK. Fast, dark and huge, it charges straight down the Liquid Rapids.

artists.name: Pharoah Sanders
artists.text: Pharoah Sanders was an American saxophonist and a towering figure of spiritual and free jazz, known for his work with John Coltrane and his own searching, devotional records. "Astral Traveling" opens his 1971 album Thembi, a gentle, floating piece built around electric piano. It is a moment of deep calm in the Old Jazz Quarter.

artists.name: Phineas and Ferb
artists.text: Phineas and Ferb is a Disney animated series created by Dan Povenmire and Jeff "Swampy" Marsh, famous for fitting an original song into nearly every episode. "Gitchee Gitchee Goo," "S.I.M.P. (Squirrels in My Pants)" and "Ain't Got Rhythm" are among its best-loved tunes, catchy and silly in all the right ways.

artists.name: Phoenix
artists.text: Phoenix are a French indie pop band from Versailles, known for crisp guitars, buoyant rhythms and Thomas Mars' smooth vocals. "Lisztomania" opens their 2009 album Wolfgang Amadeus Phoenix, which won the Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album. Bright and endlessly replayable, it lights up the Electric Fields.

artists.name: Pipetka
artists.text: Pipetka's "Hero's Ascent" is a 2023 piece in the Ambient Mists, a land of slow, drifting sound and soft light. Its title suggests a climb toward something grand, and it fits the quiet, cinematic mood of the land, music that feels like the long walk before the summit comes into view.

artists.name: PISS
artists.text: Abrasive, distorted and deliberately confrontational, PISS make noise rock. "time loop at hot slit" is a 2026 song whose strange, lowercase title matches the music's raw, chaotic spirit. It lands in the Metalcore Caldera, where its jagged noise fits among the heaviest and loudest sounds in the world.

artists.name: Pixel Terror
artists.text: Pixel Terror are an electronic duo known for heavy, melodic bass music that mixes dubstep, drumstep and future bass. "Enigma" is a 2020 track that pairs bright, emotional melodies with hard-hitting drops. It sits comfortably in the Melodic Bass Highlands, where big feelings and big bass go hand in hand.

artists.name: Pond
artists.text: Pond are a psychedelic rock band from Perth, Australia, with deep ties to Tame Impala through shared members. "Paint Me Silver" comes from their 2017 album The Weather, a glossy, synth-laden record full of shimmering hooks. Its dreamy, colourful sound fits right into the Psychedelic Wilds.

artists.name: Porch Light
artists.text: Porch Light's "Under" is a 2026 song from the Shoegaze Fens, the land of reverb, haze and slow waves of guitar. Its short title suggests sinking beneath the surface, which is just how this kind of music feels: soft, enveloping and best heard with the volume up and the eyes half closed.

artists.name: Prabh Singh
artists.text: Prabh Singh is a Punjabi singer whose music blends Punjabi pop with hip hop and modern production. "9:45," released in 2023, became a major hit, carried by a smooth, catchy hook and a laid-back groove. It brings a late-night warmth to the Velvet Rooftops.

artists.name: Primer
artists.text: Primer's "Waste Away" is a 2024 track from the Trance Steppe, a land of soaring synths, long builds and euphoric releases. Its title carries a hint of melancholy, and trance has always been good at mixing sadness with uplift, turning heavy feelings into something you can dance through.

artists.name: Prismatic
artists.text: Prismatic is the producer behind "Minty," heard here in a remix by Au5 and Fractal, two well-known names in melodic bass music. The remix balances heavy, wobbling bass with bright, glittering melody. It sits in the Dubstep Shards, where its mix of crunch and sparkle catches the light.

artists.name: Prosecutor Archangels
artists.text: Prosecutor Archangels' "Cifra palota" is a 2025 piece in the Ambient Mists, a land of slow, atmospheric sound. The title is Hungarian, meaning roughly "ornate palace," which suits music built for wandering through grand, half-imagined spaces. It is a piece to let drift while you explore.

artists.name: Pure 100%
artists.text: Pure 100%'s "BREATH" is a 2026 future bass track, full of lush chords, bright synths and soft, pulsing drops. It lives in the Melodic Bass Highlands, a land where electronic music leans emotional and airy. Its title says it all: a song that feels like a deep, slow breath out.

artists.name: Quartzone
artists.text: Quartzone makes heavy bass music that spans riddim, dubstep and melodic bass. "Supersymmetry II," from 2022, takes its name from a theory in particle physics, fitting for music built on precise, repeating patterns and huge, crystalline drops. It glints among the jagged forms of the Dubstep Shards.

artists.name: Rabbit Killer
artists.text: Rabbit Killer is an electro house producer whose tracks are made for the peak of a club night, all driving grooves and crunchy synths. "Imaginationland," from 2012, comes from the era when electro house and dubstep were trading ideas freely. It roars to life in the Electro Foundry.

artists.name: Radio Wolf
artists.text: Radio Wolf is the project of Canadian musician Oliver Blair, based in Berlin, who makes guitar-tinged synthwave full of nostalgia and big choruses. "Journeys End" is a 2020 song in that cinematic, neon-lit style. He often collaborates with the singer NINA, whose music sits nearby on the Synthwave Coast.

artists.name: Rafa
artists.text: Rafa's "Ideally Attached" is a 2020 song from the Latin Coast, a land of warm rhythms, sunny melodies and music for dancing by the sea. The title has a tender, slightly wry feel, the sound of someone figuring out a relationship, set against the easygoing glow of the coast.

artists.name: Red Vox
artists.text: Red Vox is a rock band fronted by Vinny, best known as the streamer behind Vinesauce, and they have built a loyal following through fuzzy, melodic psychedelic rock. Their songs drift between heavy riffs and dreamy, wandering passages. "Brother" carries that warm, hazy sound, the kind of track that rewards a long walk with nowhere in particular to be.

artists.name: ridgeclub
artists.text: ridgeclub makes quiet, atmospheric music that sits comfortably among the drifting sounds of the Ambient Mists. "I'm God" is a recent track, and despite its bold title it works best as a mood piece, all soft texture and slow space. It is music to let wash over you rather than study closely.

artists.name: Riot City
artists.text: Riot City is a Canadian heavy metal band from Calgary playing fast, fiercely traditional speed metal in the spirit of the 1980s. Expect galloping riffs, twin guitar leads and soaring, high-pitched vocals. "Eye Of The Jaguar" is a full-throttle example, built for raised fists and the forge fires of the Iron Range.

artists.name: Rishab Rikhiram Sharma
artists.text: Rishab Rikhiram Sharma is an Indian sitar player who comes from a family of instrument makers and has become known for his calming performances, including his Sitar for Mental Health concerts. His music draws on Hindustani classical and devotional traditions. "Chanakya" shows the patient, meditative side of the sitar, unfolding slowly and gracefully.

artists.name: Rob Gasser
artists.text: Rob Gasser is an electronic producer known for high-energy bass music that mixes dubstep weight with drumstep speed and bright, game-like melodies. His tracks became favourites on electronic labels and gaming channels in the 2010s. "Ricochet" bounces and snaps exactly the way its title promises.

artists.name: Robert Stillman
artists.text: Robert Stillman is an American saxophonist and composer whose music sits somewhere between jazz, folk and quiet experimental songwriting.
