His records favour gentle, hand-played textures and an unhurried sense of time. "It's All Is" has that reflective, open quality, a piece that feels like looking out over water at the far edge of the world.

artists.name: runfromobm
artists.text: runfromobm makes small, late-night music that fits the hushed corners of the Small Hours. "Grilled Cheese Sandwich" has a homely, offhand title that suits its mood: something comforting and low-key, the sound of being awake when everyone else is asleep. It is a modest track that feels personal rather than polished.

artists.name: Ryeland
artists.text: Ryeland is an electronic producer from the early 2010s boom in electro house and dubstep, when big drops and hard-edged synths ruled. "Luvu - Original Mix" comes from 2012 and mixes heavy bass with a lighter, playful hook. It belongs to that bright, noisy era of internet dance music.

artists.name: saddyowner
artists.text: saddyowner plays twinkly, heartfelt music rooted in midwest emo and math rock, with intricate interlocking guitars and an affectionate, nostalgic streak. "Minecraft" leans right into that nostalgia, a song whose title alone calls up long childhood afternoons spent building blocky worlds. It sits naturally among the cliffs of the Math Rock Escarpment.

artists.name: SAULT
artists.text: SAULT is a mysterious British collective that releases albums with almost no publicity, interviews or photos, letting the music speak for itself. Their sound blends soul, funk, gospel and post-punk grooves with strong themes of Black identity and resilience. "Wildfires" is one of their most affecting songs, slow, aching and quietly powerful.

artists.name: Shabazz Palaces
artists.text: Shabazz Palaces is a Seattle hip hop group led by Ishmael Butler, formerly of Digable Planets, alongside multi-instrumentalist Tendai Maraire. Their 2011 album Black Up, released on Sub Pop, was hailed for its abstract, futuristic sound. "Swerve... the reeping of all that is worthwhile (Noir not withstanding)" shows their dense, dreamlike approach to rap.

artists.name: Shady Cicada
artists.text: Shady Cicada makes alternative rock with a loose, warm feel that fits the open moors of this land. "Sweet Pea" is a gentle, tuneful song from 2018, the kind of track that sounds best with a slight breeze and a long view. It rewards anyone who enjoys guitar music that feels homemade and sincere.

artists.name: Sharpay Evans
artists.text: Sharpay Evans is the glamorous, scene-stealing drama queen of Disney's High School Musical films, played by Ashley Tisdale. "Fabulous" opens High School Musical 2 in 2007, with Sharpay lounging at her family's country club and demanding nothing less than the very best. It is pure, sparkling camp and a beloved part of the franchise.

artists.name: she
artists.text: she is an electronic artist whose bright, crisp music draws on chiptune sounds and synth-pop melody, sitting well among the machines of the Electro Foundry. "Atomic" is from 2009 and has a sleek, sparkling energy, all quick arpeggios and clean digital tones. It is upbeat music with a distinctly retro-futurist shine.

artists.name: Shred Meyer
artists.text: Shred Meyer is a recent arrival on the Isle of Memes, and the name itself is a pun worth a smile. "Bazooka" is loud, playful and doesn't take itself too seriously, which is exactly the spirit of this island. It is the kind of song that gets passed around between friends for a laugh.

artists.name: SIE Sound Team
artists.text: SIE Sound Team is the in-house music group at Sony Interactive Entertainment, credited on soundtracks for many PlayStation games. "Hunter's Dream" comes from Bloodborne, the 2015 gothic horror game, and plays in the quiet refuge where hunters rest between nightmares. It is a tender, melancholy piece that many players remember as a rare moment of safety.

artists.name: sincerely
artists.text: sincerely plays math rock with a post-hardcore edge, mixing busy, tapped guitar lines with bursts of louder, more urgent energy. "Glazey" is a 2019 track that moves between intricate, bright passages and heavier swells. It suits the jagged cliffs and switchbacks of the Math Rock Escarpment.

artists.name: Skrux
artists.text: Skrux is an electronic producer known for emotional chillstep and future bass, with big, glowing synths and heavy but gentle drops. His music found a wide audience through online electronic labels and channels in the mid-2010s. "Essence" captures that style well, soaring and bittersweet in equal measure.

artists.name: Skybreak
artists.text: Skybreak is a producer of melodic bass and dubstep, known for pairing hard-hitting low end with uplifting, cinematic melodies. "Into The Light - driftcat Remix" is a reworking by fellow producer driftcat, leaning into the track's bright and hopeful side. It feels like breaking through clouds into open sky.

artists.name: Sleepdealer
artists.text: Sleepdealer makes lo-fi hip hop beats with dusty drums, mellow samples and a relaxed, unhurried pace. "Weed" is a short, laid-back 2016 track from the era when lo-fi beats were spreading across online playlists and streams. It is background music in the best sense, ideal for drifting across the Lo-Fi Hills.

artists.name: Sonic Future
artists.text: Sonic Future makes dance music with a steady four-on-the-floor pulse, the driving kick drum at the heart of house and electronic dance styles. "Waiting For" is a 2014 track built on that hypnotic beat, with a sense of build and anticipation that suits its title. It is made for moving, not sitting still.

artists.name: Sonny Rollins Quartet
artists.text: Sonny Rollins is one of the great tenor saxophonists in jazz, famous for his huge tone, wit and gift for spontaneous melody. "St. Thomas", based on a Caribbean folk tune and first recorded on his 1956 album Saxophone Colossus, became his signature song. Its joyful calypso rhythm has made it a jazz standard ever since.

artists.name: Soulero
artists.text: Soulero makes chillstep, the gentler cousin of dubstep, where heavy bass is softened by airy pads, reverb and slow, emotional melodies. "Aura" is a 2015 track that floats more than it hits, building into a warm, spacious drop. It suits long, open journeys across the Trance Steppe.

artists.name: Sound Remedy
artists.text: Sound Remedy is an American electronic producer who first gained attention through lush, emotional remixes of indie and pop songs. His music blends chillstep and future bass with big, cinematic swells. "Medicine" is a fitting example of his healing, uplifting style, true to the name he chose for himself.

artists.name: Spacemoth
artists.text: Spacemoth makes dreamy, exploratory music that feels at home among the strange colours of the Psychedelic Wilds. With titles like "Do We Exist?" and "Telepathic Butterflies", the songs lean into cosmic wonder and gentle weirdness. They are best heard while wandering with no particular destination in mind.

artists.name: Spalexma
artists.text: Spalexma is credited with "We Are Charlie Kirk", a soulful, slow-burning ballad that spread widely online in 2025 and became a viral talking point. It is styled as a soul blues tribute, with a gospel-tinged vocal and warm backing. Its place on the Isle of Memes reflects how it circulated, as an internet phenomenon as much as a song.

artists.name: Sparky Deathcap
artists.text: Sparky Deathcap makes intimate, home-recorded indie folk with a playful and slightly eccentric spirit. "September" is a gentle 2009 song with an unpolished warmth, the kind of track that feels shared rather than performed. It fits the quiet, weathered calm of the Driftwood Shore.

artists.name: SpongeBob SquarePants
artists.text: SpongeBob SquarePants is the cheerful sea sponge of Nickelodeon's long-running animated series, voiced by Tom Kenny. "Campfire Song Song" comes from the episode where SpongeBob and Patrick go camping and try to get Squidward to join in. It starts slow, then speeds up into a frantic, joyous mess, and is endlessly quotable.

artists.name: Stage Kids
artists.text: Stage Kids play instrumental music where math rock's tricky, interlocking guitar patterns meet the swelling dynamics of post-rock. "Cyniculture" is from 2011 and moves between precise, knotty riffs and wider, more cinematic passages. It is music full of small surprises, rewarding close listening.

artists.name: Stan Forebee
artists.text: Stan Forebee makes lo-fi and jazz-tinged hip hop beats, warm and softly crackling, with mellow keys and relaxed drums. "Awakening of the Flowers" is a 2013 piece that lives up to its name, gentle and blooming. It is music for slow mornings, study sessions and lazy wandering through the Lo-Fi Hills.

artists.name: Stan Getz
artists.text: Stan Getz was an American tenor saxophonist celebrated for his smooth, lyrical tone, nicknamed "The Sound". His collaborations with Brazilian musicians helped bring bossa nova to the world. "The Girl From Ipanema", recorded with João and Astrud Gilberto and composed by Antônio Carlos Jobim, became a worldwide hit and one of the most recorded songs ever.

artists.name: Stantough
artists.text: Stantough reimagines modern hits as medieval tavern music, the style often called bardcore, using lutes, recorders and old-world arrangements. Familiar songs like "Umbrella" and "Smells Like Teen Spirit" are turned into something that sounds as if it were played in a castle hall. The joke is affectionate, and the arrangements are genuinely charming.

artists.name: StarSystems
artists.text: StarSystems plays progressive metal with djent's tight, chugging rhythms and math rock's intricate guitar work. "It's Raining on the Moon, Pt. 1" from 2016 blends heavy, precise riffing with spacey, atmospheric passages. Its title alone suggests the cosmic scale that fits the towering Djent Spires.

artists.name: Stepford Wives
artists.text: Stepford Wives makes bright, glittering music that fits the shimmer of the Glitterlands. "After Red 40" is a recent track whose title nods to the famous artificial food dye, hinting at a sugar-rush, slightly artificial sparkle. It is playful and colourful, with an edge of irony underneath the shine.

artists.name: Steph.fm
artists.text: Steph.fm makes quiet, late-night music for the hushed hours, soft and introspective. Songs like "Greyhound", "Antenna Patch" and "a second glance" feel like small scenes: bus rides through the dark, crackling radios, moments almost missed. Together they make a gentle, personal set suited to the Small Hours.

artists.name: Sunstroke
artists.text: Sunstroke brings heavy, hard-driving music to the Iron Range. "Run Away" is a 2022 track with urgent riffs and plenty of momentum, built for speed and volume. It is the kind of song that makes the forges burn a little hotter and the anvils ring a little louder.

artists.name: Super Mario 64
artists.text: This entry is a cinematic orchestral reimagining of music from Super Mario 64, the 1996 Nintendo 64 classic scored by Koji Kondo. "Bob-Omb Battlefield" is the bouncy theme of the game's very first course, and here it is reworked with a full, sweeping sound. It turns a beloved tune into something grand.

artists.name: Sweat
artists.text: Sweat makes music with a loose, hazy psychedelic feel that fits the colourful tangle of the Psychedelic Wilds. "Hilary" is a recent track, its single name giving it the feeling of a personal portrait or a half-remembered story. It is music for wandering and letting your mind drift.

artists.name: Swedish House Mafia
artists.text: Swedish House Mafia is the Stockholm trio of Axwell, Steve Angello and Sebastian Ingrosso, one of the defining acts of the 2010s progressive house boom. "Don't You Worry Child", featuring singer John Martin, was a huge international hit in 2012. Its mix of euphoric drops and heartfelt nostalgia made it an anthem of festival season.

artists.name: Sōra
artists.text: Sōra makes soft, nocturnal music suited to the quiet glow of the Small Hours. "Streetlight" captures that mood in its title alone: an empty street, a pool of light, the stillness of very late at night. It is a gentle, reflective track meant for listening alone.

artists.name: Takashi Ohmama
artists.text: Takashi Ohmama is a Japanese composer who writes music for anime, including the score for Mobile Suit Gundam: The Witch from Mercury. His work mixes orchestral drama with modern electronic textures. "Cockpit" reflects that blend, tense and driving, the sound of a pilot strapping in before something big.

artists.name: TAKIO
artists.text: TAKIO makes electronic dance music with a cosmic, driving energy, perfect for the steady pulse of the Four-on-the-Floor Steppe. "Extradimensional Cosmic Phenomenon (feat. tug)" is a recent collaboration whose title promises something vast and strange. It is music that builds and spirals, made for dancing under open skies.

artists.name: technoplanet
artists.text: technoplanet makes energetic, futuristic music with a bright, fast-moving sound that sits well among the J-Rock Isles. "Megastructure" is a 2019 track that sounds as large as its title, layered and soaring, full of sci-fi scale. It is music for neon skylines and towering imaginary cities.

artists.name: Teminite
artists.text: Teminite is an electronic producer known for heavy, aggressive dubstep and drumstep with an inventive, almost cinematic flair. His tracks have long been popular in gaming communities, especially with rhythm game fans. "Accelerate" is a 2023 release that lives up to its name, relentless and full of speed.

artists.name: The Cactus Channel
artists.text: The Cactus Channel is a soul and funk band from Melbourne, Australia, known for tight, warm instrumental grooves inspired by classic soul records. "Stay a While" is a gentle, inviting track that matches its title, the kind of slow groove that makes you want to linger. It is perfectly at home in the Funk Tropics.

artists.name: The Citizens of Halloween
artists.text: The Citizens of Halloween are the ghouls, ghosts and monsters of Halloween Town from Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas. "This Is Halloween", written by Danny Elfman, opens the 1993 film as the townsfolk proudly introduce themselves. It is a spooky, playful anthem that has become a seasonal favourite.

artists.name: The Deli
artists.text: The Deli makes lo-fi hip hop beats, built from soft jazz samples, gentle keys and laid-back, crackly drums. "Flowers" is a 2016 track from the years when lo-fi beats became the soundtrack for studying and late-night relaxing online. It is warm, simple and easy to sink into.

artists.name: The Disneyland Children's Chorus
artists.text: "It's a Small World" was written by the Sherman Brothers for the boat ride Disney created for the 1964 New York World's Fair, which later moved to Disneyland. This recording by a children's chorus captures the song's sweet, simple message of shared humanity. Famously, once you hear it, it is very hard to stop humming.

artists.name: The Duck
artists.text: "The Duck Song" is a much-loved children's song by Bryant Oden, made famous online by an animated video of a duck repeatedly asking a lemonade stand owner whether he has any grapes. Its gentle, repetitive tune and deadpan humour made it a classroom and internet favourite. It is a natural resident of the Isle of Memes.

artists.name: The Gregory Brothers
artists.text: The Gregory Brothers are an American musical group famous for Songify the News, where they auto-tune speeches and interviews into catchy songs. "Revenge by Obama (Creeper, Aw Man)" cuts together clips of Barack Obama to make him sing the beloved Minecraft parody song. It is a loving mashup of two very different corners of the internet.

artists.name: The Infield Boys
artists.text: The Infield Boys have their home on the Isle of Memes, where songs earn their place by being shared and laughed about. "I Don't Wanna Lose Your Love Tonight" is a heartfelt-sounding pop song that clearly took on a second life as an inside joke. It is best enjoyed with friends and a straight face, if you can manage one.

artists.name: The Intermezzo Orchestra
artists.text: The Intermezzo Orchestra performs recordings of popular film and television themes. Their version of the "Pirates Of The Caribbean (Main Theme)" recreates the swashbuckling music composed by Klaus Badelt and Hans Zimmer for the 2003 film. It is all galloping strings and brass, perfect for imagining a sail across open water.

artists.name: The Jauntee
artists.text: The Jauntee is a jam band from Boston, known for lively improvisation and songs that stretch and change from night to night. Their music draws on rock, funk and bluegrass, in the tradition of groups like Phish. "Valley Girl" shows their playful, easygoing side, the kind of song that opens into a long, joyful jam.

artists.name: The Lion King
artists.text: The Lion King is Disney's 1994 animated classic about the young lion Simba, with songs by Elton John and Tim Rice and a score by Hans Zimmer. These recordings include "Hakuna Matata", "Be Prepared" and "I Just Can't Wait to Be King", spanning the original and its 2019 remake. Few soundtracks are as widely loved.

artists.name: The Little Singers
artists.text: The Little Singers perform covers of classic educational songs from Schoolhouse Rock!, the beloved series of animated shorts that taught grammar, history and civics on American television. "Conjunction Junction" explains how words join together, and "I'm Just a Bill" follows a bill on its way to becoming law. Both remain cheerfully catchy.

artists.name: The Lorax Singers
artists.text: This is the ensemble credit for the songs of the 2012 animated film Dr. Seuss' The Lorax, rather than a band that tours. "Let It Grow" is the film's big closing number, a rousing, gospel-tinged sing-along in which a whole town comes round to planting trees again. It carries the story's hopeful message about caring for the natural world.

artists.name: The Mariachis
artists.text: A mariachi recording credited simply to the musicians who play it, with the trumpets, violins and guitars that define the tradition from western Mexico. Their "La Cucaracha" is a take on one of the best-known Mexican folk songs, a bouncy tune that has been sung, parodied and played on car horns for over a century.

artists.name: The Moonies
artists.text: Their "Axel F" is a take on Harold Faltermeyer's synth theme from the 1984 film Beverly Hills Cop, a melody that seemed to be everywhere again in 2005. The tune's bouncing, instantly recognisable hook made it a natural fit for remakes and novelty versions, which is how it ended up drifting through this corner of the world.

artists.name: The Muppets
artists.text: Jim Henson's troupe of felt performers has been singing since the 1950s, through The Muppet Show and a long run of films. "Rainbow Connection", written by Paul Williams and Kenneth Ascher, was first sung by Kermit the Frog in a swamp in The Muppet Movie (1979), and returned in the 2011 film The Muppets. It remains one of the gentlest songs about dreaming ever written.

artists.name: The Muppets Barbershop Quartet
artists.text: In the 2011 film The Muppets, a straw-hatted barbershop quartet of Muppet characters delivers Nirvana's grunge anthem in tight four-part close harmony. Their "Smells Like Teen Spirit" is a perfect gag: one of the angriest songs of the nineties, sung sweetly and politely, as if at an ice-cream social.

artists.name: The Simpsons
artists.text: The long-running animated family from Springfield, created by Matt Groening, also made records. "Do The Bartman", from the 1990 album The Simpsons Sing the Blues, has Bart (voiced by Nancy Cartwright) rapping over a slick new jack swing groove, and Michael Jackson was widely reported to have helped write it uncredited. It was a big hit in the UK and elsewhere.

artists.name: The Whitest Kids U' Know
artists.text: A New York sketch comedy troupe led by the late Trevor Moore, whose television show ran from 2007 to 2011 and was known for absurd, boundary-pushing humour. Their musical sketches were a highlight, and "Triumph of the Ill (Hitler Rap)" is one of the most famous: a deliberately ridiculous history-lesson rap that mocks its subject.

artists.name: The Year End
artists.text: Their "If It Hadn't Ended Then, It Would've Ended Now - 2023" pairs a long, wistful title with the restless, intricate guitar work of math rock. The genre favours tapped melodies, shifting time signatures and sudden bursts of volume, and this track sits among heavier neighbours, where those sharp edges and emotional swells feel right at home.

artists.name: They Might Be Giants (For Kids)
artists.text: This is the children's-music side of They Might Be Giants, the inventive Brooklyn duo of John Flansburgh and John Linnell, who made a whole second career of clever, warm albums for kids. "Hot Dog!" is the cheerful theme they wrote for Disney's Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, a short burst of pure joy that many listeners grew up with.

artists.name: Throttle
artists.text: Throttle is Robbie Bergin, a producer from Melbourne, Australia, known for bright, bouncy dance music. "Next Big Thing" was the track he sent to Monstercat as a teenager, and it launched his career; he went on to open for Avicii and to work with Oliver Heldens. His music is playful, upbeat and built for summer festival crowds.

artists.name: tictacto
artists.text: tictacto is a young internet producer from the dariacore scene, a hyperactive style of mashup music built from chopped-up pop and anime samples at breakneck speed. "homesick - tacto flip" is a remix, or flip, in that spirit: familiar fragments sped up, cut apart and rebuilt into something giddy, glitchy and strangely sentimental.

artists.name: tides.
artists.text: A lo-fi beatmaker in the jazz-hop tradition, making short, warm instrumentals for studying, drifting or late nights. "tuscano" is typical of the style: dusty drums, mellow jazz chords and a soft crackle, looped just long enough to settle into. It is music meant to sit quietly in the background and make a room feel calmer.

artists.name: Tim Koch
artists.text: This is glitchy, intricate electronic music in the IDM tradition, where beats are taken apart and reassembled with a watchmaker's care. "Ik Zak Fout", whose title is Dutch, moves through clipped rhythms and odd digital textures, the kind of track that rewards headphones and close listening more than the dance floor.

artists.name: Tinariwen
artists.text: Tinariwen are Tuareg musicians from the Sahara in northern Mali, formed around Ibrahim Ag Alhabib around 1980. Their hypnotic electric guitars and call-and-response singing helped bring desert blues to the world, and they won a Grammy for the album Tassili. "Cler Achel", from Aman Iman (2007), shows that trance-like, rolling sound at its best.

artists.name: Toby Fox
artists.text: Toby Fox is the American game developer and composer who made Undertale (2015) almost single-handedly, and later Deltarune. "MEGALOVANIA" is the frantic, chiptune-flavoured battle theme from the game's hardest fight, and it became one of the most recognisable pieces of video game music of its decade, covered and remixed endlessly online.

artists.name: TOTO
artists.text: Toto were formed in Los Angeles in the late 1970s by some of the most in-demand session musicians of their era. Their 1982 album Toto IV gave them "Rosanna", which won the Grammy for Record of the Year, and "Africa", a song whose rains and drums have enjoyed a remarkable second life online. Both are polished, warm and endlessly singable.

artists.name: Totorro
artists.text: Totorro are an instrumental math rock band from Rennes, France, with two guitars, bass and drums and no vocals. Their debut album Home Alone (2014) took them to stages across Europe, Japan and North America. "Chevalier Bulltoe" comes from that record: bright, twisting guitar lines and joyful, tumbling rhythms that tell a story without words.

artists.name: Troy
artists.text: Troy Bolton is the basketball star at the heart of Disney's High School Musical films, played by Zac Efron. "Bet On It", from High School Musical 2 (2007), is his big solo moment, a dramatic pop-rock number performed while storming across a golf course, torn between ambition and friendship. It became one of the series' most memorable and most parodied scenes.

artists.name: Uk Apache
artists.text: UK Apache is a British MC whose voice is stamped on one of jungle's defining records. "Original Nuttah", made with producer Shy FX in 1994, became a breakthrough hit for the genre, with its rapid breakbeats, booming bass and fearless ragga vocal. "Original Nuttah 25" marks the track's twenty-fifth anniversary, reworked for a new generation.

artists.name: unclepat
artists.text: This is an independent artist with a recent, small catalogue, placed on the quiet, weathered shoreline of the world. Songs like "Humility" and "It Doesn't Matter to Me Anymore" suggest reflective, plain-spoken songwriting, the kind that sounds best late at night, about letting go and looking honestly at oneself.

artists.name: velvet stripe
artists.text: A recent independent act whose "Haunt You Here" landed among the jam bands, where long, loose grooves and live interplay are the common language. The title hints at something moody and lingering, a song about memory and places that keep a hold on you, played with the open, wandering feel of musicians listening to each other.

artists.name: Velvetine
artists.text: Velvetine are a small international electronic group known for melodic, vocal-led trance. "The Great Divide" became best known through the Seven Lions remix released on Anjunabeats in 2012, which blends soaring trance chords and an aching vocal with the heavy, slow-motion drops of melodic dubstep. It is a touchstone of that emotional crossover sound.

artists.name: Venna
artists.text: Venna is a London saxophonist and producer from the city's thriving young jazz scene, where jazz, rap and R&B run into one another freely. "Sicily' Box" shows that blend: a smoky, melodic saxophone over laid-back beats, sitting somewhere between a late-night jazz club and a headphone hip-hop record.

artists.name: Veronica Everheart
artists.text: A recent artist working in bedroom pop and alternative R&B, the kind of intimate, home-recorded music where soft vocals meet electronic textures. Her "2222222222222222 + Climbing" joins two ideas in one track, its playful repeated-digit title hinting at something dreamy and a little unguarded, made for late evenings and headphones.

artists.name: Vexare
artists.text: Vexare's music belongs to the early 2010s wave of chillstep, which took dubstep's heavy, half-time rhythms and softened them with piano, strings and atmospheric pads. "The Clockmaker" lives up to its name, with delicate, ticking melodies and a cinematic build, while "Rattlesnakes" leans towards something more restless and bass-driven.

artists.name: Via Luna
artists.text: This is math rock with a midwest emo heart: bright, interlocking guitar lines, unusual time signatures and a sense of warmth beneath the technical playing. "Infinite Spice" has the playful title the genre loves, and the kind of sparkling, tapped guitar figures that make the style feel both intricate and deeply friendly.

artists.name: Victor Jones
artists.text: A recent, independent artist placed among the world's more unusual and hard-to-categorise sounds. "Moon Bright Rain" has an evocative, almost haiku-like title, suggesting something quiet and nocturnal, light falling on a wet night, and it sits naturally on the winding backroads where songs that fit no neat box are given room.

artists.name: Victor Wooten
artists.text: Victor Wooten is an American bassist widely regarded as one of the greatest players of his instrument, best known as a member of Béla Fleck and the Flecktones and a multiple Grammy winner. His solo music spans jazz fusion and funk with dazzling technique and a deep sense of groove. "Dc10" shows off that agile, joyful playing.

artists.name: Vincent E. L.
artists.text: This track sits on the meme side of the world, where internet humour and music meet. The song on the playlist is a short, deliberately outrageous comedy number with a profane title aimed at the fire department, the kind of over-the-top joke song that gets passed between friends because it is so absurd.

artists.name: Voilaaa
artists.text: Voilaaa is the project of French producer Bruno Hovart, also known as Patchworks, who draws on West African funk, disco, highlife and dub. "Spies Are Watching Me" has that sound: a rolling, bass-heavy groove with echoing effects and a slightly paranoid swagger, part dance floor and part late-night dub session.

artists.name: Voodoo Visionary
artists.text: Voodoo Visionary are an American jam band who mix funk, rock and psychedelia into long, danceable live grooves. "Cold Shallow Moon" shows their style: a loose, swampy rhythm section, bright keys and guitar solos that take their time, the kind of song that stretches out and changes shape from night to night on stage.

artists.name: VRIGGER
artists.text: A meme-music act from the internet's slowed-and-funky corner, where tracks are pitched down and drenched in bass for comic effect. Their song on the playlist pairs a deliberately provocative, darkly joking title with a heavy, slowed funk beat, the kind of shock-humour edit that spreads through group chats rather than radio.

artists.name: Vylet Pony
artists.text: Vylet Pony is an American electronic musician who emerged from the My Little Pony fan community and grew into an ambitious concept-album artist, mixing hyperpop, electronic music and heartfelt storytelling. "Creature City" captures that energy: bright, glittering production and big emotions, built around a vivid imagined world.

artists.name: Warrant
artists.text: Warrant were a Los Angeles glam metal band fronted by the late Jani Lane, part of the Sunset Strip scene of the late 1980s. "Cherry Pie", the title track of their 1990 album, became their signature song, a cheeky, fist-pumping party anthem with big guitars and bigger hair, and an MTV staple of its day.

artists.name: Wendy's
artists.text: This track lands squarely in metalcore, with crushing breakdowns, screamed verses and soaring clean choruses. "The Best Combo Meal on the Worst Night of my Life" features Beau Bokan, singer of Blessthefall, and its title leans into the genre's love of long, dramatic song names, here with a wink towards fast food.

artists.name: Will Backerman
artists.text: A recent, independent songwriter whose "Pawn Shop Ring" belongs among the warm, lantern-lit sounds of folk and Americana. The title alone tells a small story, of love offered on a modest budget or a keepsake that changed hands, and it suits the intimate, story-led songwriting this part of the world is made for.

artists.name: Woulg
artists.text: Woulg is Greg Debicki, a Montreal-based artist working in glitch, IDM and generative music, who has performed across Europe, the Americas and Australia. His work treats sound like sculpture, splintering rhythms into tiny fragments and reassembling them. "The Water" is a fluid, detailed example of that meticulous, shimmering style.

artists.name: Write Out Loud
artists.text: Write Out Loud is a contest for new musical theatre writers, founded in 2019 by Tony nominee Taylor Louderman and Benjamin Rauhala. "Little Miss Perfect", written by contest winner Joriah Kwamé and sung by Louderman, is a ballad about the pressure of appearing flawless, and it found a large, devoted audience online.

artists.name: wuudlum
artists.text: A lo-fi hip-hop producer making gentle, unhurried instrumentals built on soft drums, warm samples and a hint of vinyl hiss. "Häwelmann" takes its name from a German children's bedtime story by Theodor Storm about a little boy who wants to roam at night, a fitting title for music this sleepy and dreamlike.

artists.name: Wyatt Waddell
artists.text: His "Gone Away" sits along the world's garage rock strip, where songs are raw, direct and played with the amps turned up. The title suggests a song about absence or leaving, delivered with the immediacy of a band in a small room, rough edges left in on purpose and feeling worn on the sleeve.

artists.name: Yellow Days
artists.text: Yellow Days is the project of English singer and guitarist George van den Broek, who drew attention as a teenager with a deep, soulful voice far older than his years. "Gap in the Clouds" is a woozy, sun-hazed bedroom pop song, wrapping jazzy chords and lo-fi warmth around a mood that is hopeful and melancholy at once.

artists.name: YELLOW MAGIC ORCHESTRA
artists.text: Yellow Magic Orchestra, the Tokyo trio of Haruomi Hosono, Ryuichi Sakamoto and Yukihiro Takahashi, were pioneers of electronic pop whose influence reaches techno, synthpop and video game music. "RYDEEN", from Solid State Survivor (1979), is a galloping, joyous synthesiser instrumental and one of the most famous pieces of Japanese pop ever made.

artists.name: yums
artists.text: A meme-music act whose "SCOTLAND FOREVER" belongs firmly to the internet's comedy side. With its all-caps, rallying-cry title, it is the kind of over-the-top, tongue-in-cheek anthem that gets shared for laughs, half patriotic battle hymn and half joke at the expense of the whole idea.

artists.name: Yussef Kamaal
artists.text: Yussef Kamaal was the London duo of drummer Yussef Dayes and keyboardist Kamaal Williams, whose only album, Black Focus (2016), became a landmark of the city's new jazz scene. Mixing jazz fusion, broken beat and funk, tracks like "Strings of Light" and "Joint 17" feel loose, live and full of groove, and the pair split soon after.

artists.name: Zac Efron
artists.text: Zac Efron became a star as Troy Bolton in Disney's High School Musical films before moving on to a wide-ranging film career. "What Time Is It" is the bright ensemble opening of High School Musical 2 (2007), celebrating the start of summer, and "Gotta Go My Own Way" is the heartfelt duet from the same film in which Gabriella says goodbye.

artists.name: Zebbler Encanti Experience
artists.text: Zebbler Encanti Experience is an audiovisual duo of video artist Zebbler and electronic producer Encanti, whose live shows pair heavy, glitchy bass music with immersive projection-mapped visuals. Their music lives where IDM, dubstep and psychedelia meet, and "Flesh Out" shows that mix: twisting, mechanical rhythms and huge, warping low end.

artists.name: ZEOL
artists.text: This is modern bass music in the dubstep and riddim vein, with a softer, melodic side. "Iridescent" lives up to its shimmering title, pairing glowing synth melodies with heavy, wobbling drops, the kind of track that moves between beauty and weight in a few bars and rewards a good pair of speakers.

artists.name: Zero Eden
artists.text: A recent electronic artist whose songs on the playlist sit among the world's four-on-the-floor dance music. Titles like "Ocean Simulator", "Between Binaries" and "Anything Is Possible" suggest a dreamy, digital, slightly futuristic outlook, steady pulsing beats with an optimistic, almost virtual-world glow.

artists.name: zts
artists.text: An electronic artist whose "goldenslaughterer" sits on the trance plains of the world. Run together as one long, lowercase word, the title has the cryptic, internet-born feel common to underground electronic music, and the track belongs with the rising synths and hypnotic, driving pulse that trance is built on.

artists.name: 天狼群
artists.text: 天狼群 (Tenrougun) is a vocal unit of four voice actresses formed for the 2025 anime Bad Girl, a school comedy, performing as their characters. "BAD SURPRISE" is the show's ending theme, a lively, playful anime pop song that, along with their opening theme, appears on their album KING OF EVIL.

artists.name: 松澤由美
artists.text: Yumi Matsuzawa is a Japanese singer best known for anime songs, beginning with her debut single, the opening of Martian Successor Nadesico, and including themes for Saint Seiya. "Kuusou mesorogii" is her recording of a song best known as the opening of the anime Future Diary, sung here with her strong, dramatic voice.

artists.name: 楽音
artists.text: This is a recent J-pop remix, a playful reworking that brings bright, bouncy electronic production to a K-pop-adjacent source. "mosi mosi? LEESOL (KiiiKiii) Remix" takes its name from the Japanese telephone greeting, and its quick, sugary energy fits the colourful, fast-moving pop of this part of the world.
